LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights How to watch, what to know and a prediction as Jacksonville heads to Baltimore to open Week 9 Imagn Images In the Week 9 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Baltimore Ravens play host to the Jacksonville Jaguars . Baltimore is coming off a devastating loss to the Buffalo Bills in which Lamar Jackson returned from his ankle injury and was promptly injured on his first play of the game. The Ravens also lost backup Tyler Huntley during the contest, and they are now decimated on offense as they head into Thursday night's game. Jacksonville came off its bye last week and laid the smack down on the division rival Indianapolis Colts , winning 42-7 to improve to 5-2 on the season and further solidify their hold on the AFC South. Trevor Lawrence and the offense are rolling, and the defense has been largely excellent so far this year. Will the Jaguars take care of business on the road, or will the Ravens pull off a shocking upset? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Ravens vs. Jaguars live Date: Thursday, Nov. 5 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: M&T Bank Stadium (Baltimore) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Jaguars -9.5, O/U 39.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Jaguars have the ball The Jags enter this game having destroyed the Colts last week behind a monster performance from their running game. Bhayshul Tuten ran 16 times for 104 yards and a touchdown, while Chris Rodriguez carried it six times for 41 yards and another score. Rodriguez was limited in practice this week with a hand injury but will play on Thursday night. Tuten's status is up in the air after he didn't practice all week due to an ankle injury sustained against Indianapolis. He played through that injury for the rest of the game, but Jacksonville might choose to rest him here. He's a game-time decision. The Ravens are allowing only 3.8 yards per carry this season, with a mere 0.8 of those yards coming before contact, according to Tru Media. Jacksonville could have some issues running the ball, especially if Tuten is out, if the Baltimore front can hold up as it has for most of the season. The Ravens did get clocked for 146 yards on the ground this past week by the Bills, but James Cook averaged south of 4.0 yards per carry. A lot of the damage was done by Ray Davis late in the game with six carries for 30 yards. Josh Allen also chipped in 30 of his own. Trevor Lawrence obviously isn't as mobile or as involved in the run game as Allen, but he can move, and if the Ravens get out of their rushing lanes, he can make things happen as a scrambler. Lawrence has played extremely well so far this season, completing 65.7% of his passes at an average of 8.5 yards per attempt, with 17 touchdowns (and a league-high 8.6% touchdown rate) against just four interceptions. Lawrence's top target is clearly Parker Washington , who splits his time fairly evenly between lining up out wide and in the slot. The Ravens are 21st in net yards per attempt allowed this season, and their cornerbacks ( Marlon Humphrey and Nate Wiggins ) largely haven't played up to expectations. Kyle Hamilton remains excellent against both the run and pass in the slot, so one could expect Washington's route split to lean more heavily toward the outside. Jacksonville may lean toward putting him where he can line up against Humphrey, whose struggles this season have been fairly well documented. Elsewhere on the perimeter, Jakobi Meyers and, to a lesser extent, Brian Thomas Jr . and Josh Cameron are involved. Meyers and Thomas have only combined for three more targets than Washington has, though, so they are more clearly ancillary pieces in the passing game. The box-score expectations for them should be somewhat muted, but they can pop up at any time for key plays. (Thomas did score last week in his return to the full-time WR3 role, for example.) The Ravens, meanwhile, have been relatively stingy against tight ends in the passing game, allowing only 35 receptions to players at the position, so it's probably not going to be the biggest night for Brenton Strange . Tight ends do have six touchdowns against the Ravens, though, so it might be worth it to at least watch out for Strange in the red zone. When the Ravens have the ball You can throw out all of the Ravens' offensive stats. Not only is Lamar Jackson out, but so is backup quarterback Tyler Huntley. Jacoby Brissett is reportedly on the way to help, but he won't be active on Thursday night. Emergency third quarterback Joe Fagnano entered the game in relief of Jackson and Huntley last Sunday and will make the start on Thursday night. Fagnano, an undrafted free agent out of UConn, went 10-of-21 for 91 yards and an interception against the Bills. He threw most of his passes to the running backs and did not connect with Zay Flowers even once. Expect the Ravens to lean heavily on Derrick Henry and the run game, but do not expect them to find much success. Henry has been struggling of late to begin with (45 carries for 156 yards and a touchdown over the last three games combined), and the Jaguars have allowed 3.4 yards per carry this season — the single-best mark in all of football. Unless Fagnano and offensive coordinator Declan Doyle pull off some kind of magic act, the Ravens are likely not going to be able to move the ball much on Thursday night. The Ravens simply do not have the horses to compete with the Jaguars this week. Not with their third-string quarterback (who is coming off an injury of his own), and not on a short week. Jacksonville should roll and win with relative ease. Pick: Jaguars 27, Ravens 6 Now Playing Share Share Video Does Lamar Jackson-less Baltimore have any chance in 'TNF' matchup? LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images It's safe to say that last week lived up to the hype. The Detroit Lions defeated the previously undefeated Minnesota Vikings , the Denver Broncos used a goal-line stand to hand Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs their second consecutive loss, and the Chicago Bears upset the Seahawks in Seattle with some help from trade-deadline addition Jeffery Simmons . This weekend in the NFL , the Cincinnati Bengals and Atlanta Falcons will battle in Madrid, Jordan Love takes the Green Bay Packers to Foxborough to play the New England Patriots and Baker Mayfield gets a shot at Caleb Williams and the red-hot Bears. Which teams should you pick in Week 9, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 4 from DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research for its hard work. Jacksonville Jaguars (-10) at Baltimore Ravens (TNF) Dajani ( Jaguars -10): It's tough to pick this game since we are unaware of the Baltimore Ravens ' quarterback situation. Will they be starting rookie third-stringer Joe Fagnano , or someone else? I believe the Jaguars will win, but any team can cover a double-digit spread at home. Jacksonville is a remarkable 14-3 over its last 17 games and is the only NFL team leading its division by three or more games. Trevor Lawrence leads the NFL in passer rating (112.6), while the Jags lead the league in points per game differential (+12.1). Sure, you can say the Ravens will just ride Derrick Henry , but the Jaguars have what is statistically the No. 1 run defense in the NFL, and have gone 24 straight games without allowing a 75-yard rusher. … Prediction: Jaguars 28, Ravens 13 Dubin (Jaguars -10): The Ravens simply do not have the horses to compete with the Jaguars this week. Not with their third-string quarterback (who is coming off an injury of his own), and not on a short week. Jacksonville should roll and win with relative ease. … Prediction: Jaguars 27, Ravens 6 Cincinnati Bengals (-3) vs. Atlanta Falcons (Madrid) Dajani (Falcons +3): I may take the upset here. I'm aware the Falcons just registered one of the most embarrassing losses of the season in Tampa, but I'm willing to overlook that given how bad the weather was. I have some questions about the Bengals. Cornerback DJ Turner has a heel injury, and Cashius Howell just broke his wrist. Then, this Cincy defense allowed the lowly Tennessee Titans to put up 440 yards of total offense last week and allowed the first Titans' 300-yard passing game since the 2023 season. Tony Pollard rushed for 117 yards and two touchdowns, so what is Bijan Robinson going to do? Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins are the best wide receiving duo in the league, but the Bengals may be due for their first loss in over a month. Remember, this Falcons team beat the San Francisco 49ers the last time they played a game indoors. Give me the points. … Prediction: Falcons 27, Bengals 23 Dubin (Bengals -3): The Cincinnati offense is rolling, with Joe Burrow , Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins dunking on opposing defenses. Meanwhile, the Falcons have been struggling to run the ball as of late despite the presence of Bijan Robinson (48 carries for 200 scoreless yards in the last three weeks). The Bengals do provide an opportunity for the run game to get back on track (4.8 yards per carry allowed), but Dexter Lawrence has shut down other rushing attacks before. If the Bengals can keep Robinson in check, I'm not sure Atlanta can count on Michael Penix Jr . to go shot for shot with Burrow. … Prediction: Bengals 27, Falcons 20 Los Angeles Rams (-5.5) at Washington Commanders Dajani ( Rams -5.5): I think the Washington Commanders are a feisty team that could cover this number, but don't forget that this is somewhat of a revenge game for Sean McVay. He spent seven seasons in Washington before the Rams made the smart decision to hire this 30-year-old kid to run their franchise. In his first season as a head coach, McVay lost to his former team. Since then, he's 2-0 vs. Washington, winning each game by at least eight points. The Rams are coming off back-to-back wins by 14+ points. They also could get Myles Garrett back on Sunday. LA is 11-2 SU and 10-3 ATS in its last 13 games vs. teams entering below .500. … Prediction: Rams 27, Commanders 17 Dubin (Rams -5.5): The Rams have finally climbed back to .500 with back-to-back wins over the Raiders and Chargers , and I think they can keep things rolling here by doing what they did against those two teams: running the ball. Washington has actually been pretty good against the ground game this year, but it just lost Daron Payne to a significant injury. On the other side of the ball, I don't think we can count on the Commanders' offense to produce enough points to keep up with LA's offense. … Prediction: Rams 24, Commanders 16 Denver Broncos (-2.5) at Carolina Panthers Dajani (Broncos -2.5): I told you the Broncos would beat the Chiefs last week. The conversation around Bo Nix is so bizarre to me. He's not Josh Allen , obviously, but he's not worth benching either. He's not the most prolific passer in NFL history, but he's Superman when it comes to leading his team to wins in crunch time. Denver does have a great defense, which pulled off that goal-line stand vs. Kansas City, but Nix leads the NFL since 2000 with 9.1 yards per attempt when down by one score in the fourth quarter. He has 15 game-winning drives to his name, which is one shy of the most in a three-season span in NFL history. Nix hasn't even played three full seasons. It hasn't always been pretty, but Nix is pretty good in those fourth quarters. This week, Denver travels to take on the Carolina Panthers . Bryce Young 's offensive line has some serious issues, and those were evident last week against the Packers. Through Week 8, Carolina has allowed 23 sacks, which is tied for second-most in the NFL, with 11 of those sacks coming in the past two games. However, Jordan Love leads the NFL with 2,246 passing yards, while Christian Watson and Matthew Golden are the first duo to have 600 yards receiving each through eight games since Jaylen Waddle and Tyreek Hill in 2022! Drake Maye has been great, having scored at least three touchdowns over five straight games, but this Packers defense will provide quite the test. Green Bay has allowed just 14.6 points per game over its last five. … Prediction: Packers 27, Patriots 24 Dubin (Packers +3): I also think Green Bay's extra rest will matter here, even if only because it will give Christian Watson some extra time to heal up from the ribs injury he suffered last Thursday night. Meanwhile, Green Bay's defense has been excellent for several weeks now, and with the Patriots down multiple weapons in the passing game, I think the Packers can try to make New England one-dimensional here, limiting their chances to move the ball downfield. … Prediction: Packers 26, Patriots 20 Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Chicago Bears (-6) (SNF) Dajani (Bears -6): I correctly chose Chicago to cover in Seattle last week, and I became even more confident in that pick when the Bears traded for Jeffery Simmons. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Pete Prisco reveals all of his Week 9 picks, including the Bills handing the Vikings their second straight loss Imagn Images The turnaround week looked promising early Sunday. Then it went rotten — at least with my against-the-spread NFL picks , I went into the late games with a 6-3 ATS record. I ended up 7-7 for the week. That takes my season record to a horrible 50-68-3. As for my straight-up picks, I went 10-4. That brings my season record to 72-48-1. That I will take. Now it's time to get going on the ATS record. I went with some strange dogs this week in hopes of getting back on track. Let's hope they bark. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Jacksonville Jaguars (-10) at Baltimore Ravens Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime The Jaguars get a break on a short week, not having to face Lamar Jackson at quarterback. The Ravens are a different team without him and now must play rookie Joe Fagnano . Trevor Lawrence is playing at a high level and the run game is going well. Look for the Jaguars to win a road game on a short week. Pick: Jaguars 27, Ravens 16 Cincinnati Bengals (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Madrid on Sunday, 9:30 a.m. on NFL Network (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bengals have been flying high on offense with Joe Burrow throwing it around. The Falcons have struggled on offense in recent weeks, which is never a good thing when trying to keep up with Burrow. Look for a lot more big plays from the Bengals as they win this one in Spain. Pick: Bengals 33, Falcons 21 Denver Broncos (-2.5) at Carolina Panthers Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Panthers have been beat up the past two games, leading to the firing of defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero. They are reeling on defense. The Broncos won a tough one last week against the Chiefs thanks to late-game magic by Bo Nix . This time, it's a lot easier against a bad Panthers defense and struggling offensive line. Pick: Broncos 26, Panthers 20 Dallas Cowboys (-6) at Indianapolis Colts Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Cowboys are coming off a horrible loss to the Cardinals at home, but they get a big break playing the Colts , who are struggling. Indianapolis has major problems and there is talk of trading more players. The Cowboys will get the offense cranked up again in this one as they get back on track behind their passing game. Pick: Cowboys 31, Colts 17 New York Jets (+9.5) at Kansas City Chiefs The Chiefs are back home after losing two straight on the road. The Jets blew a late lead to the Raiders last week. Kansas City has not run it the past two weeks, but look for Kenneth Walker to get back on track. The Chiefs win it to break the losing streak, but the Jets and their offense hang around. Pick: Chiefs 24, Jets 17 Detroit Lions (-7) at Miami Dolphins This is a tough trip for the Lions coming off two home division victories, and it's against a young team playing much better. But this is a big challenge for the Miami defense. The Lions can score in bunches and I think they will in this one. Look for a big day from Jared Goff . Pick: Lions 30, Dolphins 13 Cleveland Browns at New Orleans Saints (-1.5) The Browns are playing consecutive road games after losing to the Steelers last week. The Saints are coming off a bye, so big advantage there. The Browns were bad on offense against the Steelers, which I think carries over here. The Saints will do enough to win a low-scoring game. Pick: Saints 17, Browns 14 New York Giants at Philadelphia Eagles (+3.5) The Giants are coming off a bye in first place in the division, while the Eagles are coming off a road loss Sunday night to the Commanders . They are struggling in many areas. But this is a big rivalry, and pride will help keep the Eagles in it, as their defense has a solid day against J.J. McCarthy . But the Giants win it late. Pick: Giants 22, Eagles 20 Los Angeles Rams at Washington Commanders (+5.5) This is a long trip for the Rams , but they seemed to have righted things the past few weeks. The Commanders rallied to beat the Eagles Sunday night. The Washington defense played well in that game, but this could be a game where Matt Stafford gets it cranked up. Jayden Daniels will play well to keep it close, but the Rams will win it. Pick: Rams 28, Commanders 24 Houston Texans at Los Angeles Chargers (+4.5) Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Texans are coming off a bye, while the Chargers are coming off a loss to the Rams. Neither team has come close to expectations before the season, with the Chargers winless. The Texans' defense and the Chargers' offense have both struggled. But I think the Chargers will hang around in this one behind their defense. Pick: Texans 19, Chargers 16 Las Vegas Raiders at San Francisco 49ers (-10) Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Raiders are playing consecutive road games, while the 49ers are coming off a bye. Big edge for the 49ers. Plus, they are the better team. The Raiders' defense is struggling, so look for Brock Purdy to have a big day throwing the football. 49ers big. Pick: 49ers 31, Raiders 17 Green Bay Packers at New England Patriots (+3.5) This has the feel of a low-scoring game with two good defenses — even though both teams have good quarterbacks. The Packers have added rest from playing last Thursday, which will help. The Patriots had to rally and beat the Dolphins last week. The defenses play well, but It's Jordan Love who makes the plays late to win it. Pick: Packers 19, Patriots 16 Arizona Cardinals at Seattle Seahawks (-12.5) The Seahawks are coming off an embarrassing home loss to the Bears , while the Cardinals won at Dallas last week. They are making a quarterback change to Gardner Minshew , who played well last week. Good luck against this Seattle defense, which will be hunting after the Bears beat them. The Cardinals will get the brunt of their anger. Pick: Seahawks 30, Cardinals 13 Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+6) at Chicago Bears Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are coming off that impressive victory over Seattle Monday night on the road. That was domination. But there might be a little letdown here. The Bucs have played impressive defense this season and have cranked up their running game. They will run it well here, but in the end, Caleb Williams will make late plays to win it. Pick: Bears 24, Bucs 21 Buffalo Bills (-3.5) at Minnesota Vikings Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This is the game of the week, featuring two of the better teams in the league. I can't wait to see the Vikings ' defense against Josh Allen . But I think the Bills will run the ball at the Minnesota defense, much like the Lions did last week. The Bills defense has been better as of late, and that will show up against a limited Minnesota offense. away.headline: Jaguars-Ravens Injury Report: Why Recent History Doesn't Bode Well for Bhayshul Tuten
away.blurb: The Jaguars released their final injury report for Thursday's Week 9 battle with the Baltimore Ravens, and it featured two big names as questionable: running back Bhayshul Tuten and defensive end Travon Walker. There is understandable concern for both, with Walker limited in practice on Tuesday and Wednesday after sustaining a rib injury in last week's win over the Indianapolis Colts. But recent history under this Jaguars regime suggests Walker has at least a chance to play. It does not say the same about Tuten. Simply put, the Jaguars will more than likely need Chris Rodriguez Jr. to step into a starting role on Thursday based on how they have handled past injury situations. Tuten did not practice on Tuesday or Wednesday, despite Jaguars head coach Liam Coen indicating in his pre-practice press conference that Tuten would have some sort of practice activity. Instead, Tuten was a DNP for the second day in a row, which has resulted in a missed game each time during the Coen era. This is the 25th game where the Jaguars are led by Coen and his staff. In the previous 24 final injury reports, the Jaguars have had 27 instances where a player did not practice during the week. In all 27 of those instances, the player missed the game that week. The key difference here is that Tuten is at least listed as questionable. All 27 previous instances of players missing practice led to them being outright ruled out, which of course has not been the case with Tuten. Coen has already tabbed Tuten as a game-time decision, something he has done two other times this year: in Week 1 with Cole Van Lanen and LeQuint Allen, who were each listed as questionable but played. The difference is that Van Lanen and Allen at least practiced that week. If this was a full week and not a Thursday Night Game, which the Jaguars have not played under Coen before, perhaps things would be different. But for now, most signs point toward Tuten not being available just simply based on the Jaguars' history under Coen. Perhaps one key that could answer the Tuten question is how Coen approached Van Lanen's status in Week 1. Van Lanen was coming off a serious knee injury that had kept him out of the entirety of training camp, though he returned in time to be limited in practice in Week 1. But a few weeks before then, here is what Coen had to say. home.blurb: Jacoby Brissett won't be on the Baltimore Ravens in time to start Thursday's game against the Jacksonville Jaguars with Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe) injured, but the plan is reportedly for him to take the field in Week 10. "That is the expectation," NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported when asked if Brissett will start against the Los Angeles Chargers on Nov. 16. Ravens to Trade for Brissett 😈 Report: Brissett Restructures Contract His update comes after he and ESPN's Adam Schefter reported the Ravens "are finalizing a trade" to acquire the veteran quarterback from the Arizona Cardinals in a move that is "expected to be completed this weekend." Baltimore came into the season with realistic Super Bowl expectations in large part because of Jackson's presence under center, but now it is in scramble mode following the injuries to its top-two quarterbacks. Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano will start Thursday's game after seeing some action in the team's most recent loss to the Buffalo Bills. He went 10-of-21 for 91 yards, zero touchdowns and one interception in defeat. As for Brissett, he was benched in the Cardinals' overtime win over the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday. Gardner Minshew II entered the game and overcame a 14-point deficit in the fourth quarter with touchdown passes to Tyler Allgeier, Trey McBride and Michael Wilson. ▶️ Full Cardinals-Cowboys Recap 06:17 With Minshew and rookie Carson Beck on the roster, Brissett became expendable. Now it seems like the veteran will be tasked with leading the Ravens back into the AFC playoff picture. They enter Thursday's game with three straight losses and a 4-4 record, which has them in last place in the AFC North. There is plenty of talent on the offense with Derrick Henry, Zay Flowers and Mark Andrews, among others, but the quarterback play will ultimately determine the team's ceiling the rest of the season. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images It's safe to say that last week lived up to the hype. The Detroit Lions defeated the previously undefeated Minnesota Vikings , the Denver Broncos used a goal-line stand to hand Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs their second consecutive loss, and the Chicago Bears upset the Seahawks in Seattle with some help from trade-deadline addition Jeffery Simmons . This weekend in the NFL , the Cincinnati Bengals and Atlanta Falcons will battle in Madrid, Jordan Love takes the Green Bay Packers to Foxborough to play the New England Patriots and Baker Mayfield gets a shot at Caleb Williams and the red-hot Bears. Which teams should you pick in Week 9, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 4 from DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research for its hard work. Jacksonville Jaguars (-10) at Baltimore Ravens (TNF) Dajani ( Jaguars -10): It's tough to pick this game since we are unaware of the Baltimore Ravens ' quarterback situation. Will they be starting rookie third-stringer Joe Fagnano , or someone else? I believe the Jaguars will win, but any team can cover a double-digit spread at home. Jacksonville is a remarkable 14-3 over its last 17 games and is the only NFL team leading its division by three or more games. Trevor Lawrence leads the NFL in passer rating (112.6), while the Jags lead the league in points per game differential (+12.1). Sure, you can say the Ravens will just ride Derrick Henry , but the Jaguars have what is statistically the No. 1 run defense in the NFL, and have gone 24 straight games without allowing a 75-yard rusher. … Prediction: Jaguars 28, Ravens 13 Dubin (Jaguars -10): The Ravens simply do not have the horses to compete with the Jaguars this week. Not with their third-string quarterback (who is coming off an injury of his own), and not on a short week. Jacksonville should roll and win with relative ease. … Prediction: Jaguars 27, Ravens 6 Cincinnati Bengals (-3) vs. Atlanta Falcons (Madrid) Dajani (Falcons +3): I may take the upset here. I'm aware the Falcons just registered one of the most embarrassing losses of the season in Tampa, but I'm willing to overlook that given how bad the weather was. I have some questions about the Bengals. Cornerback DJ Turner has a heel injury, and Cashius Howell just broke his wrist. Then, this Cincy defense allowed the lowly Tennessee Titans to put up 440 yards of total offense last week and allowed the first Titans' 300-yard passing game since the 2023 season. Tony Pollard rushed for 117 yards and two touchdowns, so what is Bijan Robinson going to do? Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins are the best wide receiving duo in the league, but the Bengals may be due for their first loss in over a month. Remember, this Falcons team beat the San Francisco 49ers the last time they played a game indoors. Give me the points. … Prediction: Falcons 27, Bengals 23 Dubin (Bengals -3): The Cincinnati offense is rolling, with Joe Burrow , Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins dunking on opposing defenses. Meanwhile, the Falcons have been struggling to run the ball as of late despite the presence of Bijan Robinson (48 carries for 200 scoreless yards in the last three weeks). The Bengals do provide an opportunity for the run game to get back on track (4.8 yards per carry allowed), but Dexter Lawrence has shut down other rushing attacks before. If the Bengals can keep Robinson in check, I'm not sure Atlanta can count on Michael Penix Jr . to go shot for shot with Burrow. … Prediction: Bengals 27, Falcons 20 Los Angeles Rams (-5.5) at Washington Commanders Dajani ( Rams -5.5): I think the Washington Commanders are a feisty team that could cover this number, but don't forget that this is somewhat of a revenge game for Sean McVay. He spent seven seasons in Washington before the Rams made the smart decision to hire this 30-year-old kid to run their franchise. In his first season as a head coach, McVay lost to his former team. Since then, he's 2-0 vs. Washington, winning each game by at least eight points. The Rams are coming off back-to-back wins by 14+ points. They also could get Myles Garrett back on Sunday. LA is 11-2 SU and 10-3 ATS in its last 13 games vs. teams entering below .500. … Prediction: Rams 27, Commanders 17 Dubin (Rams -5.5): The Rams have finally climbed back to .500 with back-to-back wins over the Raiders and Chargers , and I think they can keep things rolling here by doing what they did against those two teams: running the ball. Washington has actually been pretty good against the ground game this year, but it just lost Daron Payne to a significant injury. On the other side of the ball, I don't think we can count on the Commanders' offense to produce enough points to keep up with LA's offense. … Prediction: Rams 24, Commanders 16 Denver Broncos (-2.5) at Carolina Panthers Dajani (Broncos -2.5): I told you the Broncos would beat the Chiefs last week. The conversation around Bo Nix is so bizarre to me. He's not Josh Allen , obviously, but he's not worth benching either. He's not the most prolific passer in NFL history, but he's Superman when it comes to leading his team to wins in crunch time. Denver does have a great defense, which pulled off that goal-line stand vs. Kansas City, but Nix leads the NFL since 2000 with 9.1 yards per attempt when down by one score in the fourth quarter. He has 15 game-winning drives to his name, which is one shy of the most in a three-season span in NFL history. Nix hasn't even played three full seasons. It hasn't always been pretty, but Nix is pretty good in those fourth quarters. This week, Denver travels to take on the Carolina Panthers . Bryce Young 's offensive line has some serious issues, and those were evident last week against the Packers. Through Week 8, Carolina has allowed 23 sacks, which is tied for second-most in the NFL, with 11 of those sacks coming in the past two games. Plus, the Panthers' defense has allowed an incredible 42.7 points per contest in their first three home games, which eventually led to the firing of defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero last week. … Prediction: Broncos 24, Panthers 20 Dubin (Broncos -2.5): I'm not buying into Nix as much as Dajani is, but I am buying into Denver's defense being able to get after Bryce Young behind what is an increasingly leaky offensive line and preventing the Panthers from denting the scoreboard. If they can keep this a low-scoring game, I like them to pull out a win on the road. … Prediction: Broncos 23, Panthers 17 Green Bay Packers at New England Patriots (-3) Dajani (Packers +3): The Packers got some extra rest following their Thursday win over Carolina, while the New England Patriots couldn't run away from the Miami Dolphins . This Packers offense has been fun to watch — not counting the ground game, which has registered the fewest rushing yards (485) by a team above .500 through eight games in NFL history. However, Jordan Love leads the NFL with 2,246 passing yards, while Christian Watson and Matthew Golden are the first duo to have 600 yards receiving each through eight games since Jaylen Waddle and Tyreek Hill in 2022! Drake Maye has been great, having scored at least three touchdowns over five straight games, but this Packers defense will provide quite the test. Green Bay has allowed just 14.6 points per game over its last five. … Prediction: Packers 27, Patriots 24 Dubin (Packers +3): I also think Green Bay's extra rest will matter here, even if only because it will give Christian Watson some extra time to heal up from the ribs injury he suffered last Thursday night. The Packers are going to need him against New England, even if he ends up drawing shadow coverage from Christian Gonzalez , as that will just open things up for Matthew Golden and Tucker Kraft . Meanwhile, Green Bay's defense has been excellent for several weeks now, and with the Patriots down multiple weapons in the passing game, I think the Packers can try to make New England one-dimensional here, limiting their chances to move the ball downfield. … Prediction: Packers 26, Patriots 20 Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Chicago Bears (-6) (SNF) Dajani (Bears -6): I correctly chose Chicago to cover in Seattle last week, and I became even more confident in that pick when the Bears traded for Jeffery Simmons. The Seahawks' addition of Quenton Nelson is a great one, but I think the addition of Simmons is even better. Still, with the Bengals' defense continuing to struggle, the early betting lines suggest another potentially high-scoring affair. According to FanDuel Sportsbook , Cincinnati opened as a 3.5-point favorite over Atlanta, with the Bengals listed at -225 on the moneyline and the Falcons at +188. The opening over/under was set at 49.5 points. The latest FanDuel odds show Cincinnati remaining a 3.5-point favorite, although the price has shifted to -102 for the Bengals and -120 for the Falcons. The Bengals' moneyline has moved to -184, while Atlanta's stands at +154. The over/under has increased by one point to 50.5. The Bengals enter the matchup following a wild 43-36 overtime victory over Tennessee that featured five touchdown passes and three interceptions from Burrow, who ultimately delivered the winning score by scrambling nine yards around left end for just the second offensive overtime touchdown in franchise history. But while Cincinnati's offense once again demonstrated its ability to put points on the scoreboard, the defense raised serious questions. The Bengals surrendered 36 points in regulation to a Tennessee team that entered Sunday's game with just one victory, delivering a performance that looked disturbingly similar to the defensive struggles that plagued Cincinnati throughout last season. Atlanta, meanwhile, is coming off a 16-0 shutout loss to a Tampa Bay Buccaneers squad that did not complete a single pass. That sets up an intriguing matchup between a Falcons offense that couldn't find the end zone and a Bengals defense that had difficulty keeping the Titans out of it. But a motivated Bengals team that wants to prove it is better than last week's overtime win over the Titans will take care of business, covering the 3-point spread by plenty.

away.blurb: Bengals officially declare one player out, another questionable for Week 8 matchup against Titans Skip to content The Cincinnati Bengals released their third and final injury report ahead of their Week 8 matchup against the Tennessee Titans. Cincinnati has officially declared one player out, and another questionable for Sunday's game against Tennessee. Safety Kyle Dugger (quad) is officially out, and linebacker Joe Giles-Harris (calf) is officially questionable against the Titans. Coach Zac Taylor said at the beginning of the week Dugger would not play and is “week-to-week” after aggravating his calf injury last week against the Baltimore Ravens. Giles-Harris figures to be a game-time decision, and his status may be foreshadowed depending on whether or not the club elevates LB Emany Johnson off the practice squad Saturday. As expected, Ja'Marr Chase (ankle) is good to play despite missing Wednesday. Defensive tackles Jonathan Allen, B.J. Hill, and Dexter Lawrence II all had standard rest days. Running back Tyjae Spears (knee), wide receiver Carnell Tate (shoulder), and punter Tommy Townsend (left knee) have all been declared out. None of them practiced at all this week, including Tate, the former Ohio State Buckeye and No. 4 overall pick from the 2026 NFL Draft. WR Calvin Ridley (hip) is questionable. Assuming he plays, it'll be him, Elic Ayomanor, and Wan'Dale Robinson leading quarterback Cam Ward's passing attack with Tate sidelined. Starting tight end Gunnar Helm may also see a rise in involvement. He caught four passes for 24 yards last week against the Cleveland Browns. DT John Franklin-Myers (groin) is also questionable, along with cornerback Jaylon Jones (knee), and LB Dorian Mausi (foot). Mausi is still on the Reserve/Injured list and is ineligible to play unless Tennessee activates him to its 53-man roster. The Cincinnati Bengals are riding high after their second consecutive victory. They'll look to make it three in a row as they return home to face the Tennessee Titans. Mayfield guided the Bucs to their second win of the season against the Carolina Panthers in Week 7, and oddsmakers are buying the Buccaneers at home in Week 8 against the Atlanta Falcons. The Buccaneers are favored to win their matchup with the Falcons, sitting as 2.5-point favorites in the odds at DraftKings Sportsbook . After a 1-5 start to the season, Tampa Bay's win over Carolina thrust it back into the mix to win the division this season. Another win over an NFC South opponent would go a long way for Tampa Bay getting into the playoffs, and the running game has really stepped forward in recent weeks with both Mayfield and Jalon Daniels under center. Mayfield wasn't asked to do much against Carolina, completing just seven of his 11 passes for 76 yards and a score. He's completed 63.6 percent of his passes for 679 yards, three scores and two picks in four games. Daniels led Tampa Bay to one win while Mayfield was sidelined, but it's pretty clear that oddsmakers view the former No. 1 overall pick as a major upgrade under center. Mayfield and the Bucs take on Altanta and Chicago over the next two weeks before their bye. Atlanta is currently one game ahead of Tampa Bay in the NFC South, but a win on Sunday would vault the Bucs into second in the divison, just a half-game back of the Panthers (3-4). home.headline: Bengals defense gets great news during first real practice in Spain ahead of international game against Falcons
home.blurb: Cornerback DJ Turner II (heel) was a full participant Thursday, which is huge news for the Bengals defense. Turner, who left during Sunday's win against the Tennessee Titans , was classified as day-to-day with his heel injury and would not have practiced Wednesday if they did practice. He was expected to be limited Thursday, as implied by coach Zac Taylor, but went full instead. He's absolutely on track to play against Atlanta. Defense end Cedric Johnson (ankle/foot) was limited Thursday. Johnson also left the Titans game and did not return, but with a full practice Friday, he should be good to go. If he's limited, he may be a game-time decision. Johnson is one of Cincy's primary backup DEs, and with rookie Cashius Howell now on I.R , he's likely the new first guy off the bench. Safety Kyle Dugger (quad) aggravated his quad injury during Week 7 and is still week-to-week. Defensive tackle Jonathan Allen got his gotten his usual rest day. S Jordan Battle is still limited with the same hamstring injury he's been playing through for the last month. The Falcons had their first real practice out in Madrid, and made zero changes to their injury report. DE Billy Bowman Jr. (hamstring), linebacker Devine Deablo (forearm), and running back Brian Robinson Jr. (hamstring) all missed Atlanta's Week 8 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers due to their respective injuries. Bowman went full while Deablo and Robinson were limited. Wide receiver Zachariah Branch (hamstring) remains a non-participant. Dallas is coming off a crushing 33-30 overtime loss to Arizona in which it led 24-10 early in the fourth quarter and 30-24 in the final minute, only for Gardner Minshew to lead an 80-yard game-tying touchdown drive before Chad Ryland won it with a 42-yard field goal in overtime. Dak Prescott completed 19 of 29 passes for 195 yards and a touchdown and added a five-yard rushing score, but Dallas managed only 261 total yards and went three-and-out on its lone overtime possession. The loss dropped the Cowboys to 3-5 and magnified a season-long problem: the defense. Dallas is allowing 26.6 points and 385.4 yards per game. The bigger issues for Indianapolis are on the offensive side of the ball where the Colts average just 20.1 points per game. Yes, it seemed obvious the Colts were waving the white flag following midweek trades of DeForest Buckner and Quentin Nelson but to make sure there was no doubt of their intentions, they endured a smack from Jacksonville on Sunday, 42-7. The Jaguars led 28-0 at halftime and finished with 366 total yards, while the Colts’ offensive woes were on full display turning the ball over three times and amassing a mere 243 yards. Daniel Jones endured a particularly rough afternoon, finishing 19-of-28 for 144 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions, including a 92-yard pick-six, before Anthony Richardson replaced him late. Reports Monday indicated that Jones is expected to remain the starter against Dallas, with Richardson staying in the backup role. Sunday’s game is beyond a must-win for Dallas if they are to continue to entertain any hopes of even competing for a playoff spot. The Colts’ offense has been pedestrian on its better days, but the Cowboys have made even bad offenses look elite. The most recent meeting between these teams produced one of the wildest quarters in Cowboys’ history. On December 4, 2022, Indianapolis trailed 21-19 entering the fourth quarter in Arlington before Dallas erupted for 33 unanswered points to win 54-19. Prescott threw three touchdown passes, Tony Pollard ran for 91 yards and two scores, and the Cowboys forced five turnovers, including Malik Hooker’s 38-yard fumble-return touchdown against his former team. The recent series has otherwise gone back and forth: Indianapolis shut out Dallas 23-0 in 2018, Dallas won 42-7 in 2014, the Cowboys earned a 38-35 overtime victory in 2010, and Dallas won 21-14 in 2006. away.blurb: Sunday’s matchup at Lucas Oil Stadium brings together two teams badly in need of a reset, as the Dallas Cowboys (3-5) visit the Indianapolis Colts (2-6) at 1 p.m. ET. Dallas is coming off a crushing 33-30 overtime loss to Arizona in which it led 24-10 early in the fourth quarter and 30-24 in the final minute, only for Gardner Minshew to lead an 80-yard game-tying touchdown drive before Chad Ryland won it with a 42-yard field goal in overtime. Dak Prescott completed 19 of 29 passes for 195 yards and a touchdown and added a five-yard rushing score, but Dallas managed only 261 total yards and went three-and-out on its lone overtime possession. The loss dropped the Cowboys to 3-5 and magnified a season-long problem: the defense. Dallas is allowing 26.6 points and 385.4 yards per game. The most recent meeting between these teams produced one of the wildest quarters in Cowboys’ history. On December 4, 2022, Indianapolis trailed 21-19 entering the fourth quarter in Arlington before Dallas erupted for 33 unanswered points to win 54-19. Prescott threw three touchdown passes, Tony Pollard ran for 91 yards and two scores, and the Cowboys forced five turnovers, including Malik Hooker’s 38-yard fumble-return touchdown against his former team. The recent series has otherwise gone back and forth: Indianapolis shut out Dallas 23-0 in 2018, Dallas won 42-7 in 2014, the Cowboys earned a 38-35 overtime victory in 2010, and Dallas won 21-14 in 2006. Meanwhile, Marist Liufau has also returned to full participation as he works through his 21-day return-to-practice window, potentially giving Dallas another option at linebacker. The secondary is another area worth monitoring. Caleb Downs and P.J. Locke both progressed from not participating Wednesday to limited participation Thursday while dealing with concussions, an encouraging sign for Dallas. Both players must complete the NFL's concussion return-to-participation protocol. Their return to practice is encouraging, but neither is guaranteed to be available Sunday. Joey Porter Jr. also went from a full participant on Wednesday to limited on Thursday with an ankle injury. With multiple defensive backs dealing with injuries, Dallas could be facing some significant depth concerns against Indianapolis. At tight end, Jake Ferguson has missed the first two practices of the week with an ankle injury, leaving his availability for Sunday in question. Luke Schoonmaker has been limited in consecutive practices while dealing with a groin injury, but his participation is an encouraging sign. Getting Schoonmaker back would be particularly important if Ferguson remains sidelined, as Dallas could otherwise be severely shorthanded. The Cowboys also have some questions at wide receiver, where George Pickens has been limited for two consecutive days with a hamstring injury. His continued participation is encouraging, but his status will be worth monitoring ahead of Friday.

home.headline: Cowboys Injury Blow: Malachi Lawrence Out Weeks Before Colts
home.blurb: Cowboys Injury Blow: Malachi Lawrence Out Weeks Before Colts Home Safety Jalen Thompson is on injured reserve with a hamstring injury. Schottenheimer said his practice window is not open yet. Wide receiver and returner KaVontae Turpin has been out with a rib injury and missed the Arizona game. Lawrence was the 23rd overall pick out of UCF. He has 13 tackles, 3 quarterback hits, and a sack in eight games, and he took over a starting outside linebacker spot three games ago. On Monday, Schottenheimer said Lawrence’s injury was “a little different” from the other ankle injuries Dallas came out of the game with. FRISCO, Texas — Linebacker Dee Winters was set to do individual work at practice Wednesday, Dallas Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said, and tight end Luke Schoonmaker was expected to work back into practice. Rookie outside linebacker Malachi Lawrence is still looking at an absence of a few weeks with the ankle injury he suffered in Sunday’s 33-30 overtime loss to the Arizona Cardinals . Dallas plays at the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday, and Schottenheimer said the staff will make decisions after two more days of information. “Get a few guys back rolling along a little bit. Again, Dee Winters, you’ll see him do some individual today. Joey should do good,” Schottenheimer said. “Schooney should be working back into practice. Fergie will be doing some stuff with the trainers. And then both Caleb and PJ are still in the protocol. And then Turp’s still working to continue his rehab. And then Malachi Lawrence is going to probably be a few weeks. So get some more information over the next two days and make a decision.” Winters strained his Achilles in the Oct. 18 loss at the Green Bay Packers and was listed with a calf injury on the injury report. He missed the games against the Philadelphia Eagles and Arizona. Schoonmaker was inactive Sunday with a groin injury after missing practice that week. Cornerback Joey Porter Jr. played through an ankle injury Sunday. Dallas acquired him in a trade with the Pittsburgh Steelers earlier this season. Tight end Jake Ferguson hurt his ankle in the first quarter against Arizona and did not finish the game. Caleb Downs, P.J. Locke Remain In Concussion Protocol Safety Caleb Downs , the 11th overall pick in April, left Sunday’s game in the fourth quarter. Safety P.J. Locke played Sunday for the first time since coming off injured reserve, after missing five games with a foot injury. Downs leads the Cowboys with 30 tackles. Malachi Lawrence Had Started The Last Three Games “It’s just, again, we know it’s going to be a few weeks, so that’s what we’re looking into,” Schottenheimer explained. The Cowboys’ active outside linebackers without Lawrence are Rashan Gary , Donovan Ezeiruaku , James Houston , Von Miller , and Tyrus Wheat . Dallas sacked Arizona quarterbacks 5 times Sunday, 2 of them by defensive tackle Quinnen Williams . The Cowboys are giving up 152.8 rushing yards per game, and Arizona ran for 202 on Sunday.

Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton The New York Jets head to Arrowhead Stadium on Sunday, November 8, trying to keep their season from slipping further away against a Kansas City Chiefs team that is looking to halt a skid of its own. The Jets have lost three straight. They are 2-6 overall (1-3 on the road) and approaching the cellar in the AFC East. The Chiefs are 3-0 at home and 5-2 overall but have lost two in a row and sit in second in the AFC West a ½ game behind the Broncos. The Jets are coming off a frustrating 38-33 home loss to the Raiders in which they produced plenty of offense but couldn’t stop Vegas late. New York scored on its first six possessions, led 23-14 at halftime and 30-21 during the third quarter, but Las Vegas rallied with back-to-back touchdown drives to take a lead late. Geno Smith threw for 290 yards, two touchdowns and an interception, while Braelon Allen rushed for a career-high 147 yards and a touchdown and Adonai Mitchell produced a career-best 142 receiving yards with a score. A big red flag for the Jets continues to be their inefficiency in the red zone on offense and defense: New York went just 2-for-6 in the red zone while Las Vegas finished 4-for-4. Kansas City also melted late in their game last Sunday against the Broncos, blowing a 24-13 fourth-quarter lead in a 28-24 loss at Denver. Patrick Mahomes played much better than he had in the Chiefs’ previous defeat at Seattle, completing 30 of 41 passes for 321 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions, including a 73-yard touchdown to Emmett Johnson . Denver, however, scored 15 unanswered points in the fourth quarter, Harrison Butker missed a 54-yard field goal, and after Mahomes drove the Chiefs inside the Broncos’ 5 in the final minute, Denver made a goal-line stand capped by Malcolm Roach’s sack on fourth down. Historically, the matchup has produced some memorable games. The most recent meeting was a few years ago on October 1, 2023, when Kansas City escaped MetLife Stadium with a 23-20 win. The Chiefs raced ahead 17-0 in the first quarter before the Jets rallied to tie the game at 20 behind Zach Wilson , who completed 28 of 39 passes for 245 yards and two touchdowns. Mahomes had an unusually uneven passing night, finishing 18 of 30 for 203 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions, but Kansas City retook the lead on Butker’s 26-yard field goal and Mahomes used his legs to help drain the clock late. That game offers a useful blueprint for Sunday’s upset-minded Jets: withstand Kansas City’s early punch, keep Mahomes from creating explosives and turn offensive production into touchdowns rather than field goals. For the Chiefs, the larger storyline is whether they can rediscover their finishing touch after consecutive losses on the road. picks.headline: Chiefs-Jets betting line & game prediction: KC looks to get back on track
picks.blurb: Read our AI Policy. The Chiefs enter Sunday as 9.5-point favorites against the Jets at Arrowhead. Kansas City seeks to revive its ground game behind Kenneth Walker and Emmett Johnson. The prediction picks the Chiefs to beat the Jets 24-13 and cover the spread. The Kansas City Chiefs and New York Jets both need a win. Last week, the Chiefs suffered their second straight loss as the Denver Broncos rallied from an 11-point fourth-quarter deficit to win 28-24. The Jets suffered their third consecutive loss Sunday, falling 38-33 to the Las Vegas Raiders. How to watch Chargers at Chiefs Kickoff: Noon Central Time Where: Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City TV: CBS (Channel 5 in Kansas City) Radio: KFNZ (96.5 FM in Kansas City, KNSS 98.7 FM in Wichita) Betting line: Chiefs -9.5. Behind the NYJ-KC matchup Although their goals and expectations entering the season were different, Sunday’s Chiefs-Jets game represents a fork in the road for both teams. The Chiefs entered 2026 hoping to rebound from a 6-11 season and return to the Super Bowl conversation, but their loss to Denver has turned simply winning the division into a dogfight. At the same time, Jets head coach Aaron Glenn needs to show tangible progress in his second season — or his tenure in New York could be short-lived. A home matchup against the two-win Jets presents the Chiefs with the classic get-right opportunity. Their best path to doing so lies in reestablishing the ground game. New York is 21st in the league against the run in opponent yards per game (123.6), allowing 4.0 yards per carry. During his first five games, Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker averaged 133 rushing yards per game. Walker rushed for just 105 yards combined in the losses to Seattle and Denver, but he still ranks third in the NFL with 770 rushing yards. Kansas City will also look for ways to involve rookie Emmett Johnson more after his breakout performance of 143 scrimmage yards against the Broncos. “He’s a super-talented player, and he just brings joy,” quarterback Patrick Mahomes said of Johnson. “He has the right mindset, the right energy, and he wants to be great. Obviously, we have Kenneth, and he’s such a special football player — but to have someone that can come in whenever Kenneth’s tired or needs a break at all, and he can bring energy and juice, too, I think that’s a special combination those guys have there.” Mahomes suggested the Chiefs need to find additional touches for Johnson, potentially through an expanded role in the passing game. Johnson’s 73-yard receiving touchdown highlighted Mahomes’ 321-yard, three-touchdown performance in the loss. Kansas City’s passing game also saw a breath of fresh air with wide receiver Rashee Rice’s return to the lineup. Rice caught a team-high seven passes on eight targets for 53 yards and a touchdown against Denver. He also appeared to have the game-winning touchdown late in the fourth quarter before the play was nullified by a false-start penalty . Reestablishing the ground game with Walker and Johnson could create opportunities for Rice, tight end Travis Kelce and wide receiver Xavier Worthy against a veteran Jets secondary that has recorded just one interception this season. Still, Chiefs head coach Andy Reid respects Glenn’s defensive scheme and personnel. “They’ve got some good veteran guys — whether it’s the safeties, the linebackers,” Reid said. “So you’re not going to have things that are botched up. Sometimes, you get coverages that are kind of messed up a little bit and there are holes there. They do a good job of making sure they can adjust to most things and do it accurately. And they’ve got some guys on the front that are good football players, big guys.” A Jets player to watch is rookie pass rusher David Bailey, who missed his team’s Week 8 game because of a groin injury. Bailey leads the Jets with 5.5 sacks, more than a quarter of the team’s 20 sacks this season. Reid said there’s a “good chance” left guard Kingsley Suamataia returns to the starting lineup after being benched for the second time in four games because of a “coach’s decision.” The Chiefs’ short-yardage and goal-to-go woes have been under criticism this week after a loss in Denver could have been different by dialing up a quarterback sneak. Perhaps this is the week Reid adds it back into the playbook at long last. Despite New York’s disappointing season, quarterback Geno Smith has put together his own resurgence, entering Sunday with 1,913 passing yards, 12 touchdowns and just three interceptions. Smith has posted a passer rating above 100 in five of his last six road games, and the Jets have gained 377 and 439 yards of offense in their past two games. Against a quarterback playing so efficiently, the Chiefs will need to generate more pressure than they did against the Broncos. Pro Football Focus credited Kansas City with just five pressures against Denver’s Bo Nix. While wide receiver Garrett Wilson’s status remains in concussion protocol, running back Breece Hall could return after missing five games. In Hall’s absence, Braelon Allen has been a fantastic replacement, recording at least 100 scrimmage yards in the last four consecutive games. Wide receiver Adonai Mitchell, acquired by New York from Indianapolis in the trade that sent Sauce Gardner to the Colts, established a career high with 142 receiving yards and a touchdown against the Raiders. Chiefs cornerback Mansoor Delane missed Sunday’s game after aggravating his shoulder injury but returned to practice in a limited capacity Wednesday. Delane’s return is more important given Smith has been brilliant at throwing the deep ball, with 565 yards gained on passes of 20-plus air yards. Defensive end George Karlaftis said Wednesday that coordinator Steve Spagnuolo has preached the importance of developing a “killer instinct” after his unit’s forgettable recent fourth quarter. “No matter what the call is, you just got to find a way to finish,” Karlaftis said. “So I think, especially against a divisional opponent, against a great team that Denver is, when you’re up, when you’re leading, no matter what that lead is, you got to find a way to win the game as a defense. “And I know I felt that. I know the guys in the room, players and coaches, really felt that. And I think that’s something we’re going to take with us and harp on for the rest of the season.” Reid confirmed Wednesday that Harrison Butker will remain the Chiefs’ kicker against the Jets despite his 54-yard miss against Denver. Butker had made three extra points and a 45-yard field goal before pushing his final kick wide right. The Chiefs can get back on the right path and build some confidence by handling the Jets. The problems — an inconsistent pass rush, short-yardage struggles and too many penalties — have been glaring. This is a good opponent to fix all three against. Jets-Chiefs game prediction Beyond the Chiefs’ advantages in record, quarterback and overall outlook, I think this matchup gives Kansas City an opportunity to tap back into the offensive identity that worked early in the season — establishing Walker on the ground to open up everything else. Defensively, clean up the penalties and get to the quarterback. We’ve heard plenty about pressures, but Smith has been sacked 23 times this season — tied for second-most in the NFL. If not Sunday against the Jets, then when? The Chiefs use their get-right game to do just that. away.headline: Jets announce concerning injury update on WR Garrett Wilson
away.blurb: The New York Jets could be without their No. 1 wide receiver weapon in Sunday’s Week 9 matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs. When speaking to reporters on Wednesday, Jets head coach Aaron Glenn announced that Garrett Wilson is in the NFL ‘s concussion protocol and considered “day-to-day” moving forward. “Garrett, he’s in the concussion protocol. He’ll be day-to-day,” Glenn said. Wilson, who’s been openly frustrated about his role in the Jets’ offense so far this season, had six catches for 83 yards in this past Sunday’s 38-33 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders. Wilson’s practice status later this week will be a good indication of his potential availability for Sunday’s road matchup against the Chiefs. Fortunately for the Jets, wide receiver Adonai Mitchell is back from injury and performing at a high level. In Sunday’s loss to the Raiders, he paced New York with seven catches for 142 yards and a touchdown. Rookie pass catcher Omar Cooper Jr. has also flashed brilliance on a few occasions in his debut campaign. Sunday’s Week 9 matchup against the Chiefs will kick off at 1 p.m. ET from Arrowhead Stadium. While the Lions are shaking off some early-season mistakes, they've strung together three wins, including back-to-back wins in their division, while the Dolphins are in the early stages of a rebuild under their latest regime. The folks over at FanDuel Sportsbook have set the opening betting line at Lions -7 points . The Dolphins made a general manager and head coaching change this offseason, firing GM Chris Grier and coach Mike McDaniel after four unsuccessful seasons and hiring Jon-Eric Sullivan as their new GM and former Green Bay Packers defensive coordinator Jeff Hafley as their new coach. Like most new regimes, the new staff got to work early, cutting veteran contracts, including quarterback Tua Tagovailoa, wide receiver Tyreek Hill, and edge rusher Bradley Chubb. They also traded away former first-round pick Jaylen Waddle for a trio of picks to use in the 2026 NFL Draft to help them with the rebuild. Step one in establishing a new foundation was signing Malik Willis as their new signal caller—who most recently played in Green Bay with Hafley—and drafting six (!) rookie starters, including first-round picks guard Kadyn Proctor and corner Chris Johnson, as well as second-round pick linebacker Jacob Rodriguez, third-round receivers Chris Bell and Caleb Douglas, and fifth-round safety Michael Taaffe. As you would expect with a young roster at the beginning of a rebuild, the Dolphins have struggled out of the gate. In Week 1, the Raiders beat them by two touchdowns; the 49ers won by three touchdowns the week after; and the Chiefs beat them by two touchdowns in Week 3. The Lions trailed 7-6 at halftime before Jahmyr Gibbs broke loose for a 30-yard touchdown in the third quarter. Minnesota regained the lead at 15-12 with 8:44 remaining, but Jared Goff responded by directing a seven-play, 69-yard drive and finding Jameson Williams for the go-ahead seven-yard touchdown with 4:35 left. Goff finished 18-of-25 for 176 yards, one touchdown and one interception, while Gibbs carried 23 times for 153 yards and a touchdown and Williams caught four passes for 70 yards including the decisive score. away.headline: NFL-Lions report positive progress for linebacker Campbell after injury
away.blurb: "Preliminary indications are positive and out of respect for Jack and his family we will not share further information at this time," the team said in a statement. Nov 2 (Reuters) - Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell continues to rest and recover at a local hospital, the NFL team said on Monday, a day after he was carried off the field with a frightening injury during a game against the Minnesota Vikings. Campbell lay motionless on the ground after levelling a hit on Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson early in the fourth quarter at Ford Field and was taken to hospital after medical staff removed him from the field. The Pro Bowl linebacker, a captain for the team this season, was drafted by the Lions in the first round three years ago and coach Dan Campbell described him as the consummate teammate. "You get voted captain, that says a ton," said coach Campbell. "He earned every bit of that. He's trustworthy, he's dependable, he'd give you the shirt off his back. He's just all heart, man, all effort." (Reporting by Amy Tennery in New YorkEditing by Christian Radnedge)

Both the Dolphins and Lions released their first injury reports for the week on Wednesday. The Lions, who beat the Minnesota Vikings in Week 8, estimated their injury report after holding a walkthrough rather than a full practice. Jaylen Wright does not practice The Dolphins' second-string running back missed practice with a quadriceps injury. While Wright's contributions on offense have been minimal this year, picking up just 41 yards on 22 carries, he has been strong as a kick returner, where he is averaging 27.6 yards per kick and has a long of 79 yards. Dolphins rookie guard Kadyn Proctor fully participated in Wednesday's practice but remains in the league's concussion protocol, according to head coach Jeff Hafley. "He is progressing in the protocol," Hafley said. Jarrett Kingston, an August waiver claim from the Houston Texans for Miami, started in Proctor's place last week. Good news from Detroit's Jack Campbell The Lions' All-Pro linebacker sustained an ugly injury against the Vikings after tackling tight end T.J. Hockenson. Caught in an awkward position, Campbell hit Hockenson and had his head compress back onto his neck. He fell to the turf and lay motionless before being carted off the field and taken to a hospital. Campbell released a statement on Wednesday, indicating that he is progressing well in his recovery from the injury ( via Pride of Detroit ) : My family and I want to sincerely thank everyone for the overwhelming amount of love, prayers, and support we've received over the past few days. It means more to us than words can express. I'm incredibly encouraged by the progress I've made in such a short period of time. I have full movement in my lower body, and I'm continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body. I know there's still work ahead, but I remain very optimistic. home.blurb: Detroit listed 10 players on Wednesday's injury report , including four who were estimated as nonparticipants and five who were limited. Among those listed were Jack Campbell, Cade Mays, D.J. Reed, Brian Branch, Kerby Joseph, and Amon-Ra St. Brown. Brian Branch, Kerby Joseph Among Five Limited Players Detroit also listed five players as limited participants Wednesday, including several important defensive contributors. Branch's limited designation is worth monitoring after he and Wonnum were both ruled out of Sunday's game with concussions following a helmet-to-helmet collision. His progression through the league's concussion protocol will be important as Detroit prepares for Miami. Joseph also appeared on the report as limited with a knee injury, although Dan Campbell said on his Tuesday radio appearance that the safety will not play against the Dolphins . "Kerby will be in practice this week," Campbell said. "We're going to try to give him some scout team reps. He's not going to play this game." The Lions continue taking a cautious approach as the safety works his way back toward game action. St. Brown's appearance with a rib injury is another situation to watch. While he was listed as limited, Wednesday's designation alone does not indicate whether his availability for Sunday is in jeopardy. The team's own report spells it out: "The Lions conducted a walkthrough on Wednesday. Practice participation designations for that day are based on estimations." Detroit's situation should become clearer once the team holds a full practice. That makes Thursday and Friday particularly important, especially for players dealing with concussions and those hoping to return from injuries suffered against Minnesota. The Lions are preparing to face Miami with several key players dealing with injuries on both sides of the football. With four estimated nonparticipants and five limited players Wednesday, Detroit's depth could be tested once again. The biggest concerns involve Jack Campbell's recovery, Cade Mays' availability, and the health of Detroit's defensive backfield. The next two injury reports should provide a much clearer picture of who will be available when the Lions take the field Sunday in Miami. Watson took a big hit in the first quarter of Sunday's loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers, but he was cleared to return to the game. Deshaun Watson has been placed in concussion protocol pic.twitter.com/ViiyRHMct8 As a result, the Browns are now 3-point underdogs on the road against the Saints in Week 9. Cleveland opened as a 2.5-point underdog in Week 9, so this move is either a sign that oddsmakers think Watson will still have a shot to play Sunday, or it shows how little a gap there is between Watson and backup Shedeur Sanders. The former Colorado star briefly played in Week 8 against Pittsburgh, and Sanders started several games as a rookie during the 2025 season. The Browns are coming off of a bad loss to the Steelers, but it looks like they'll have a change at quarterback this week (forced by injury) with Shedeur Sanders being under center. The Saints are well-rested, coming off of a bye. Note that some of the picks below were written up before the Browns' quarterback news. Here is what the national media is saying about the Week 9 game between the Browns and Saints: NFL.com (Various) Why Brooke picked the Saints: Shedeur Sanders is in line to start for the Browns with Deshaun Watson, who was playing his best ball since 2020, entering concussion protocol earlier this week. The biggest difference with Sanders under center appears to be his willingness to stretch the field, as his 7.1 air yards per target in 2025 are more than Watson's 6.7 mark through eight games this season. Sanders is also working with a better receivers than he did a year ago with rookies Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion earning big roles in Todd Monken's offense. None of that will ultimately matter if the run game is dormant — as it was last week (34 yards) in Pittsburgh. The Saints' defense has been anything but great against the run, allowing 139.4 rush yards per game (29th in the NFL) and have given up north of 100 yards in all but one game in 2026. But I do see this being a get-right game for the Saints on all fronts fresh off the bye. Changes were made to the run game ( firing run-game coordinator T.J. Paganetti, signing RB Audric Estimé) and the kicking ranks (Charlie Smyth is expected to handle kicking duties after Daniel Carlson's release), and the entire roster got a little healthier. First-round receiver Jordyn Tyson returned to practice and could be a boon — if he indeed makes his NFL debut — for Tyler Shough opposite Chris Olave. Getting Kelvin Banks Jr. back along an O-line that has struggled to keep Shough clean in the pocket should also benefit Kellen Moore's unit. Sanders can smile all he wants, but the Saints will get the last laugh Sunday. The Browns were bad on offense against the Steelers, which I think carries over here. The Saints will do enough to win a low-scoring game. CBS Sports (John Breech) – Browns 20, Saints 17 Sporting News (Vinnie Iyer) – Saints 23, Browns 20 The Browns are quickly regressing to the mean and going into a hostile environment to face a hungry, young team after a bye doesn't bode well. New Orleans will have emphasized the need to execute better at home for both Kellen Moore and Brandon Staley. Tyler Shough gets it done, having more reliable weapons than Deshaun Watson. Sporting News (Bill Bender) – Saints 20, Browns 17 Both offenses are struggling. Deshaun Watson has taken a league-high 33 sacks, and the Browns average 97.6 rushing yards per game. New Orleans has been worse on the ground, but a bye week comes at the right time. The Saints are 0-4 S/U this season – and this game is a candidate for a walk-off field goal either way. at the Caesars Superdome brings together two teams in very different positions, as the Cleveland Browns (5-3) take the field against the New Orleans Saints (2-5). Cleveland is third in the AFC North but just one game behind the first place Steelers. New Orleans has lost four of their last five games and sit last in the NFC South, but they are also only a game out of first as they return from their bye. The Superdome, however, has not been kind to the Saints who are winless in four home games (0-4). Cleveland, however, is a respectable 2-3 on the road this season. Plenty of positives happening with the Browns this season, but last week’s performance is not one of them. The Steelers thumped Cleveland, 27-6, in Pittsburgh. Cleveland was held without a touchdown for the first time this year, lost two fumbles, rushed for only 34 yards and surrendered eight sacks, while the Steelers piled up 200 yards and three touchdowns on the ground. Forced to throw for much of the afternoon, Deshaun Watson completed 27 of 39 passes for 324 yards without an interception and Harold Fannin Jr. caught 10 passes for 154 yards. New Orleans has not played in a couple weeks, but their last game was also a loss to the Steelers, 16-10, in Paris on Oct. 25. The Saints managed only 18 rushing yards and were shut out in the second half, but quarterback Tyler Shough produced an encouraging performance through the air, completing 30 of 38 passes for 278 yards, one touchdown and one interception. It was symptomatic of the season to date: the offense has no balance. Historically, Cleveland leads the all-time series 13-7, but New Orleans has won each of the last three meetings, including the most recent matchup at this same venue on November 17, 2024. That game was tied 14-14 entering the fourth quarter before the Saints exploded for 21 unanswered points to win 35-14. Taysom Hill was the difference-maker, rushing seven times for 138 yards and three touchdowns, including fourth-quarter scoring runs of 33 and 75 yards, while Derek Carr threw for 248 yards and two touchdowns. Jameis Winston threw for 395 yards and two scores for Cleveland, but the Browns failed to turn their yardage into enough points. Two years later, the central question is similar for both clubs: which offense can translate production into touchdowns? Cleveland needs to protect Watson and rediscover a ground game that disappeared in Pittsburgh, while New Orleans needs Shough, Kamara and an offense coming out of the bye to take advantage of a Browns defense that just surrendered 200 rushing yards. Let’s dive into the numbers and see if we can’t find an additional sweat or two. away.headline: Browns injury updates: Harold Fannin Jr.'s groin issue adds concerning new wrinkle
away.blurb: Harold Fannin Jr., the Browns’ star tight end who’s been playing his best football as of late, was added as a limited participant due to a groin injury. Fannin was not listed with an injury on Wednesday, which signals that he may not have been able to finish Thursday’s session. Quarterback Deshaun Watson logs second straight DNP Both Williams and Barber returned to practice in a limited capacity on Thursday, so they appear to be trending in a positive direction. Collins’ workload on Friday could be telling. Wide receiver Denzel Boston (calf) and linebacker Carson Schwesinger (ankle) were both limited participants for the second straight day. They should be fine for Sunday’s game barring a setback. The Cleveland Browns’ Thursday practice report included a name the team definitely can’t afford to lose . Potentially complicating matters is that a groin injury is what cut Fannin’s rookie season short in 2025 and forced him to miss just about the entire voluntary portion of the Browns’ offseason program this past spring. The Browns only have one other tight end on their active roster in veteran Blake Whiteheart. Rookie Carsen Ryan was waived by the team on Thursday for the second time this season. Head coach Todd Monken is scheduled to speak to the media after practice on Friday, and Fannin’s health will likely be a top talking point — among some other health concerns. As expected, Watson was listed as a nonparticipant in Thursday’s practice as he continues to work his way through the NFL’s five-step concussion protocol . Watson entered the protocol on Tuesday after self-reporting symptoms to the team on Monday night. Shedeur Sanders led practice in Watson’s absence for the second straight day, and offensive coordinator Travis Switzer sounded like a man who expects Cleveland’s backup quarterback to play — and play well — in Sunday’s game in New Orleans. “I’m just excited to see him go play and hopefully let it rip,” Switzer said, “which I think he’ll do.” Rookie Emmanuel McNeil-Warren pops up on injury report with a hip issue McNeil-Warren was another Thursday addition to Cleveland’s practice report with a hip injury. The second-round rookie defensive back has played in all eight games this season for the Browns with three starts. Cleveland does have the luxury of a deep safety group, but the Saints have a strong passing attack led by quarterback Tyler Shough and wide receiver Chris Olave and McNeil-Warren figures to be part of the defensive game plan. The former Toledo standout has also been a valuable special teams contributor this season, so the team would feel his absence if Thursday’s injury proves to be serious enough to miss Sunday’s game. Veteran defensive tackle Maliek Collins remains sidelined with an elbow injury Collins missed his second straight practice on Thursday. away.headline: Cleveland Browns Injury Report Heading Into Week 8
away.blurb: Let's take a look at some of the injuries the Cleveland Browns have dealt with throughout the 2026 NFL season, looking at both sides of the ball and who is out short- and long-term. The Browns will be without Jenkins for their Week 8 game against the Steelers, and he's required to miss at least four games before becoming eligible to return. For Week 8, the Browns are relatively healthy, with only two players listed as questionable: cornerback Myles Harden and safety Daniel Thomas . Harden suffered a hamstring injury during the Browns' Week 7 but returned to the game. He was limited in practice throughout the week and is questionable against Pittsburgh. Thomas was also limited throughout the week with an ankle injury and carries a questionable designation. Howard suffered a concussion during Cleveland's Week 7 win against Tennessee and missed all three practice sessions this week. The Browns initially listed him as questionable on Friday but announced Saturday that he had cleared concussion protocol, which is a big relief considering the strength of Pittsburgh's defensive line. Flash forward heading into Week 9, and it couldn't be more opposite with the Giants as the front-runner to win the NFC East for the first time in 15 years, last doing so when the franchise won its fourth Super Bowl in 2011.
