The Giants are coming off a bye in Week 8 after a stunning 27-21 overtime victory as 10-point underdogs on the road over the Houston Texans . On the other sideline, the Eagles are off to their worst (2-6) in more than a quarter century, with their current six-game losing streak being the longest since President Barack Obama was reelected for a second term in 2012. Our NFL prognosticators are: Art Stapleton ( Giants /NFL writer, NorthJersey.com), Bert Bainbridge (sports trending reporter/columnist, NorthJersey.com), Brian Marron (digital producer, NorthJersey.com), Chris Iseman (Rutgers writer, NorthJersey.com), Mike Dougherty (sports writer, lohud.com), Bob Jordan (sports editor, Asbury Park Press/APP.com) and Dave Rivera (sports editor, USA TODAY Northeast/NorthJersey.com). Giants vs Eagles Week 9 predictions, staff standings Art Stapleton: 4-2-1 Dave Rivera: 3-3-1 Bert Bainbridge: 2-4-1 Chris Iseman : 2-4-1 Bob Jordan: 2-4-1 Brian Marron: 2-4-1 Mike Dougherty: 1-5-1 Can the Giants continue their stranglehold on the East or will the Birds losing ways finally come to an end with an upset at home over Big Blue? Art Stapleton The pick: Giants 27, Eagles 23 Here's why: John Harbaugh's team had a great bye week, with Dallas' stunning overtime defeat to Arizona increasing Big Blue's lead in the NFC East without even playing. QB J.J. McCarthy was outstanding in his first start against the Texans, clicking downfield with WR Malik Nabers, who had his fourth straight 100-yard receiving game. The Giants have not won in Philadelphia since Tom Coughlin was head coach in 2013, and they have not scored an offensive TD there in a win since their Super Bowl season of 2011. It's time for the streak to end. Bert Bainbridge The pick: Giants 30, Eagles 17 Here's why: No one thought this would be the reality at the midway point of the season with the Giants in the driver seat in the NFC East and the Eagles in free fall mode. Fresh off a bye, the G-Men go into Philadelphia and defeat the Birds at Lincoln Financial Field for the first time in 13 years. The pick: Giants 27, Eagles 16 Here's why: The Eagles are spiraling as the key injuries continue to mount, especially on offense. The Giants are the better team right now, and are fresh off of a bye week. Expect Big Blue to earn a relatively comfortable win. The pick: Giants 34, Eagles 20 Here's why: The Eagles are a mess right now and that's a big reason why the Giants are in prime position to win the NFC East. The pick: Giants 23, Eagles 16 Here's why: The Eagles are going nowhere this season, and with the Cowboys and Commanders not showing to be real threats in the NFC East at this point, John Harbaugh and the Giants are seizing the opportunity. Mike Dougherty The pick: Giants 27, Eagles 17 Here's why: After six consecutive losses, Eagles coach Nick Sirianni vowed his team would keep fighting. Those are not words usually heard in early November. A high-intensity start by the Giants should remove any drama from this one. The pick: Giants 22, Eagles 19 Here's why: J.J. McCarthy may not be Y.A. Tittle but doesn't have to be with Harbaugh's spiffy after-a-bye record (15–3, best among modern era head coaches with at least 10 games). picks.headline: Eagles-Giants Game Preview: 5 questions and answers with the Week 9 enemy
picks.blurb: Eagles-Giants Game Preview: 5 questions and answers with the Week 9 enemy - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football TNF: Jaguars-Ravens preview Wemby makes NBA history Ronaldo retires from Portugal Luka gets fan booted First CFP rankings Eagles-Giants Game Preview: 5 questions and answers with the Week 9 enemy PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 26: Jalen Carter #98 of the Philadelphia Eagles sacks Jaxson Dart #6 of the New York Giants during the third quarter in the game at Lincoln Financial Field on October 26, 2025 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images Brandon Lee Gowton · SB Nation Thu, November 5, 2026 at 7:19 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Six straight losses for the Philadelphia Eagles. Can the Birds snap the streak against the New York Giants, a division foe they've owned for a long time? In order to preview this Week 9 NFC East matchup, I reached out to our enemies over at Big Blue View . The earnest Ed Valentine kindly took the time took the time to answer my questions about this upcoming battle. Let's take a look at the answers. [For my answers to Ed's questions about the Eagles, stay tuned to BBV .] 1 – The Giants are off to their most encouraging start to a season in a long time. What has John Harbaugh specifically contributed to this team's turnaround? Credibility. That is the first word that comes to mind. He had 15 winning seasons in 18 years in Baltimore, and he didn't have to prove himself to anyone. He has driven the Giants hard and made them believe they have earned the right to win because of what they have done. I think this piece I wrote on Tuesday is instructive. Harbaugh isn't afraid to challenge players or to step on toes to make the Giants better. 2 – J.J. McCarthy's playing time has been limited but he's shown some promise. To what extent is there confidence in him moving forward this season? I don't know that there is confidence. There are, of course, already fans willing to trade Jaxson Dart and run with McCarthy next year. It is way too early for that, though. I think the best word is "excitement." The Giants did not give up on the season when Dart was lost. They went out and traded for McCarthy, which delivered the message they were not throwing in the towel. McCarthy has shown arm talent and mobility in 5 quarters. He gives them more upside than Jameis Winston. His skillset allows them to run the offense the way they designed it for Dart. Can he keep it up? Can he force the Giants into a Dart-McCarthy debate this offseason? I don't know, 3 – Who are the some of the more underrated Giants players this season? Perhaps some for the Eagles to keep an eye out for in this game? That's hard, honestly. Rookie WR Malachi Fields is developing nicely. Bryan Hudson has taken the center job away from John Michael Schmitz. Abdul Carter doesn't have big sack numbers, but he has been hell to block all season. Deonte Banks has been playing well, really well. He looked like a No. 1 shutdown cornerback in Week 7 against Nico Collins of the Texans. 4 – What's the biggest matchup in the Giants' favor and the biggest matchup against their favor? The run defense has been hit and miss. Saquon Barkley hitting the home run still scares me. The Giants are solid against the run, until they aren't. When they aren't, they give up big plays. Other than that, the thing that scares me is that I still think the Eagles defensive front can dominate games. 5 – Who wins this game and why? With the Giants currently listed as 3-point road favorites (first time they've been favored in Philly since 2009), what's your score prediction? With great trepidation, I will pick the Giants to win. I'm still wrapping my head around the Giants being favored. They were 10.5-point underdogs two weeks ago in Houston. They have not won in Philly since 2013, and I am well aware that bad things always seem to happen to the Giants at the Linc. I have said for year, though, that at some point things have to turn around. I think this is the year they finally do. I will say Giants 24, Eagles 17 .

picks.headline: Giants at Eagles: Predictions, picks and odds for NFL Week 9 game
picks.blurb: The Giants and Eagles approach midseason on divergent paths within the division. The Eagles have lost six straight games, yet the team is resisting further change as it tries to navigate the rest of the season without Jalen Hurts. The Giants, meanwhile, have embraced adapting on the fly, most notably with the switch to J.J. McCarthy as the starting quarterback. McCarthy built a good deal of confidence in his first start with the Giants. After the bye, he could have an even more complete command of the offense, though Vic Fangio's defense could test his patience and precision. Is there any way up for an Eagles offense that has already reached rock bottom? Philadelphia ranks 30th in scoring and last in yards per game. Saquon Barkley has indicated he won't be dealt at the deadline, but even the 2024 Offensive Player of the Year looks incapable of rescuing this severely shorthanded crew. Eagles vs Giants odds, moneyline, over/under Opening lines: Spread: Giants -3.5 Moneyline: Giants -170; Eagles +150 Get the edge with our exclusive NFL betting picks Eagles vs Giants USA TODAY expert picks Adam Kaufman: Giants 23, Eagles 17 The Giants are favored in Philadelphia. We haven't seen that since 2009! New York comes off its bye with an opportunity to strengthen its position in an NFC East that apparently nobody else wants to win. The Eagles' offense has struggled without Jalen Hurts, and Tanner McKee needs considerably more help than he's getting. At every level. Cam Skattebo's availability matters for Big Blue, but Malik Nabers gives J.J. McCarthy a receiving threat capable of changing a possession in a hurry. New York hasn't won in Philadelphia in its last 13 tries, but couldn't be getting the home team at a better time. Michael Middlehurst-Schwartz: Giants 26, Eagles 17 This feels like it could reinforce the new world order within the NFC East. The Eagles' offensive woes show no signs of abating, and Abdul Carter could wreak havoc against an overmatched offensive line. J.J. McCarthy should be able to muster enough of a spark to guide Big Blue against a Vic Fangio defense that seems like a shell of past versions of itself. Nicholas Brinkerhoff: Giants 20, Eagles 13 There will be no style points awarded in this game. The Giants are fresh off a bye week and will soon find out if J.J. McCarthy turned into a pumpkin over Halloween. The Eagles are battered and bruised, leaving Philly wondering if it can just fast forward to the offseason. John Harbaugh's Giants are in complete control when it comes to the NFC East race and should have no difficulty defeating the Eagles after making the trip down the turnpike. 'Big Blue” takes care of business. Philadelphia (2-6). That is 17 years in the making, and the spread of Giants -3 is no mistake; the Eagles are trying to get out of the gutter. Philadelphia has lost six straight games, and only two of them have come by single-digit margins. The Eagles have a bye week following this NFC East clash, and I’m sure they feel it couldn’t come soon enough. Tanner McKee will make his fourth consecutive start after leading the Eagles to 14, 21, and 10 points. The offense has been injury-riddled. DeVonta Smith sat out and Saquon Barkley hobbled to 30 yards and a touchdown on 13 carries. Makhi Lemon had another strong game with six catches for 57 yards, but there wasn’t much to brag about in the 27-10 loss. The Eagles jumped out to a 10-0 first-quarter lead, then allowed a 27-0 run. Philadelphia ranks 30th in points per game (17.1), last in yards per play (4.4), and 24th in third-down percentage (37.2%). No matter how good the defense is, the offense has shown they are incapable of going score for score without Jalen Hurts . One could argue that the best thing to happen for the Giants’ season is J.J. McCarthy . The New York offense has scored 27 points in each of the last two games and could’ve been 2-0. However, the Giants lost to the Saints 34-27 and beat the Texans 27-21 in OT before the bye week. New York has a rest advantage and likely a mental advantage over Philly. The Giants should be feeling good as they sit atop the NFC East, whereas the Eagles are at the bottom. As the first half of the season wraps up, the most surprising stat of the Giants might be that they rank eighth in total yards allowed at 313.0 per game. The New York defense will have its first shot of the season against a depleted Philadelphia offense, and coming off a bye week, it couldn’t have come at a better time. Let’s dive into the numbers and see if we can’t find an additional sweat or two. away.headline: Eagles injury report: 7 players miss practice ahead of Giants game
away.source: USA TODAY Touchdown Wire on MSN
away.blurb: The Eagles have already placed Dameon Pierce and Tank Bigsby on injured reserve, leaving Jaydon Blue and other available options to shoulder the workload if Barkley cannot play. Outside linebacker Jonathan Greenard was limited with an ankle injury, while Jalyx Hunt was limited because of knee and ankle issues. Both players will be worth monitoring as Philadelphia prepares to face the Giants. Offensively, guard Landon Dickerson (hip) and tight end Dallas Goedert (knee) practiced fully. McKee was also listed as a full participant despite a chest injury, while kicker Jake Elliott was limited with a right ankle injury. The Eagles will return to practice Thursday, and Friday's final injury report will provide a clearer picture of player availability for Sunday's matchup. The Philadelphia Eagles returned to the practice field Wednesday with several significant injury concerns ahead of Sunday's Week 9 matchup against the New York Giants . Philadelphia listed 18 players on its initial injury report, including seven who did not participate in practice. Running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring/back), linebacker Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad), defensive back Michael Carter (abdomen), wide receiver Britain Covey (knee), cornerback Jonathan Jones (hamstring), wide receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) were all sidelined. The extensive injury report comes as the Eagles attempt to snap a six-game losing streak and improve on their 2-6 record before entering their Week 10 bye. Philadelphia is particularly thin at running back and wide receiver, creating another challenge for an offense preparing to make a quarterback change from Tanner McKee to Joe Milton. Saquon Barkley, DeVonta Smith among seven sidelined Barkley's status remains one of Philadelphia's biggest concerns after the veteran running back has continued to deal with hamstring and back injuries. His absence Wednesday raises questions about the Eagles' backfield options against the Giants. Philadelphia's receiving corps is also dealing with significant injury problems. Smith and Wicks both missed practice Wednesday, while Covey remained sidelined with a knee injury. The potential absence of multiple receivers would create additional challenges for Milton, who is preparing to make his first start with Philadelphia after replacing McKee. Defensively, Campbell and Jones were among the players unable to participate. Carter also missed practice with an abdominal injury, leaving Philadelphia with more questions about its defensive depth. Eagles receive encouraging updates on defense. Despite the lengthy list of absences, the Eagles received some encouraging news with several key defensive players participating in practice. Linebacker Zack Baun was a full participant despite a shoulder injury, while defensive tackle Jordan Davis practiced fully with a thumb injury. Defensive tackle Moro Ojomo (neck) and defensive back Kenny Moore II (glute) also participated without rest

away.headline: Giants WR Malik Nabers responds to concerns after sudden injury update
away.blurb: Nabers held no injury designation earlier this week and was a full participant on Wednesday. However, he logged a “DNP” designation on Thursday’s injury report. New York Giants superstar wide receiver Malik Nabers sparked some concern regarding his health on Thursday, working with trainers off to the side of the practice field. When asked about his lack of practice participation on Thursday, Nabers pumped the breaks on concerns regarding his status for Sunday’s Week 9 matchup against the division-rival Philadelphia Eagles. “I’ll be good,” Nabers told reporters. Nabers has been absolutely stellar through the Giants’ last four games, reeling in 36 catches for 509 yards and two touchdowns over that span. On Thursday, the NFL recognized him as the NFC Offensive Player of the Month for October. Nabers wasted no time developing chemistry with new quarterback JJ McCarthy. In McCarthy’s first start with the Giants in Week 7, Nabers secured seven of his nine targets for 111 yards in an overtime win over the Houston Texans. Fresh off their Week 8 bye, the Giants will kick off against the Eagles at 1 p.m. ET on Sunday. away.headline: Giants WR Malik Nabers reveals game status after missing practice
away.blurb: New York Giants star wide receiver Malik Nabers sat out of the team’s latest practice on Thursday due to a knee injury. However, he’s confident it won’t sideline him for the Giants Week 9 matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles. According to Jordan Raanan of ESPN, Nabers told reporters that he will be good to go for Sunday’s game. It certainly allows for a sigh of relief as the Giants continue to fend off the rest of the NFC East in first place with a 4-2-1 record. The Dallas Cowboys are in second place at 3-5, Washington Commanders in third at 2-4-1 and Eagles in last at 2-6. There’s no overstating how much Nabers means to New York’s offense as he has already racked up 48 receptions for 605 yards and two touchdowns this season. If Nabers were to ever have to miss any time, the Giants wide receiver corps would become a big concern with rookie Malachi Fields and veterans Darnell Mooney, Charlie Jones and Gunner Olszewski next in line. The Giants are already without starting quarterback Jaxson Dart for the rest of the season after he suffered a multi-ligament left knee injury in Week 2, so Nabers has and will continue to play a very big role in elevating the play of whoever is at quarterback. The Giants will issue an official designation for Nabers on Friday, so all eyes will be peeled when that injury report is released. The No. 6 overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft, Nabers has recorded 175 catches for 2,080 yards and 11 touchdowns in his professional career. We talk about trying to win football games. And if that gives us the best opportunity to win a football game. We're talking about one rep. The New York Giants took the field on Thursday for their third of four practices ahead of a Week 9 game against the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, this Sunday at 1:00 p.m. ET. home.headline: Eagles injury report: 7 players miss practice ahead of Giants game
home.source: USA TODAY Touchdown Wire on MSN
home.blurb: The Eagles have already placed Dameon Pierce and Tank Bigsby on injured reserve, leaving Jaydon Blue and other available options to shoulder the workload if Barkley cannot play. Outside linebacker Jonathan Greenard was limited with an ankle injury, while Jalyx Hunt was limited because of knee and ankle issues. Both players will be worth monitoring as Philadelphia prepares to face the Giants. Offensively, guard Landon Dickerson (hip) and tight end Dallas Goedert (knee) practiced fully. McKee was also listed as a full participant despite a chest injury, while kicker Jake Elliott was limited with a right ankle injury. The Eagles will return to practice Thursday, and Friday's final injury report will provide a clearer picture of player availability for Sunday's matchup. The Philadelphia Eagles returned to the practice field Wednesday with several significant injury concerns ahead of Sunday's Week 9 matchup against the New York Giants . Philadelphia listed 18 players on its initial injury report, including seven who did not participate in practice. Running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring/back), linebacker Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad), defensive back Michael Carter (abdomen), wide receiver Britain Covey (knee), cornerback Jonathan Jones (hamstring), wide receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) were all sidelined. The extensive injury report comes as the Eagles attempt to snap a six-game losing streak and improve on their 2-6 record before entering their Week 10 bye. Philadelphia is particularly thin at running back and wide receiver, creating another challenge for an offense preparing to make a quarterback change from Tanner McKee to Joe Milton. Saquon Barkley, DeVonta Smith among seven sidelined Barkley's status remains one of Philadelphia's biggest concerns after the veteran running back has continued to deal with hamstring and back injuries. His absence Wednesday raises questions about the Eagles' backfield options against the Giants. Philadelphia's receiving corps is also dealing with significant injury problems. Smith and Wicks both missed practice Wednesday, while Covey remained sidelined with a knee injury. The potential absence of multiple receivers would create additional challenges for Milton, who is preparing to make his first start with Philadelphia after replacing McKee. Defensively, Campbell and Jones were among the players unable to participate. Carter also missed practice with an abdominal injury, leaving Philadelphia with more questions about its defensive depth. Eagles receive encouraging updates on defense. Despite the lengthy list of absences, the Eagles received some encouraging news with several key defensive players participating in practice. Linebacker Zack Baun was a full participant despite a shoulder injury, while defensive tackle Jordan Davis practiced fully with a thumb injury. Defensive tackle Moro Ojomo (neck) and defensive back Kenny Moore II (glute) also participated without rest

home.headline: Giants RB Cam Skattebo Misses Practice With Hamstring Injury Ahead of Eagles Game
home.blurb: There’s obviously an extra motivating factor for Skattebo to be ready for Sunday’s game against Philadelphia because last year’s ankle injury happened on the Lincoln Financial Field turf, and for him to return to the scene of the crime and post another career day that matches or tops his Houston performance (17 carries, 124 yards, one touchdown) would bring his comeback full circle. If Skattebo isn’t at least limited in the next day or two, it might make sense for him to sit out Sunday’s game so he’s ready for the clash against the Commanders on Thursday night. NFL Week 7 Winners and Losers: Seahawks Spoil Kenneth Walker III’s Return to Seattle Giants RB Cam Skattebo Misses Practice With Hamstring Injury Ahead of Eagles Game Skip to main content SI.COM New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo (hamstring) tops the team’s Week 9 injury report after missing Wednesday’s practice. Skattebo was injured on his 42-yard run in overtime against the Houston Texans two weeks ago. At the time, he tried to downplay the injury, but head coach John Harbaugh later characterized the running back as “day to day up to the game,” and said, “We’re just going to have to see where we’re at.” Where things stand doesn’t look very promising, as hamstrings are tricky injuries and Skattebo’s absence from practice has raised concerns for the Giants, especially since Tyrone Tracy Jr. is currently on injured reserve with his own hamstring injury, also suffered in the game against the Texans. Skattebo undoubtedly doesn’t want to miss any more time, especially after losing most of his rookie campaign last year to an ankle injury. If Skattebo can’t go, the Giants will likely turn to Devin Singletary as their lead back. They also have Greg Desrosiers on the roster, whom they signed off the Los Angeles Chargers practice squad last week, and they will likely elevate either Phil Mafaha or Eric Gray, the latter signed this week to the practice squad, for Sunday’s game. "I feel very confident about the running back situation. I like the guys we've got," Harbaugh said. "Obviously, Motor (Devin Singletary) has been here. We've got some guys that have been here in the past, too, that we brought in, as you know, that were here, and we also brought in one, (running back) Eric (Gray). "So, I feel good about it. We claimed a guy off the Chargers (Gregory Desrosiers). He's a very talented, young guy. So, those guys are in practice. They've got two practices now, and if they have to go, they'll definitely be ready to roll." While it’s too soon to say for certain what Skattebo’s status will be for Sunday, keep in mind that the Giants have a short work week following their game against Philadelphia. Sitting Sunday would give him a few extra days to get right for that game, and a longer break afterward to make more progress on his hamstring. picks.blurb: Week 10 Preview: Los Angeles Rams vs Washington Commanders - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football TNF: Jaguars-Ravens preview Wemby makes NBA history Ronaldo retires from Portugal Luka gets fan booted First CFP rankings Week 10 Preview: Los Angeles Rams vs Washington Commanders | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Sue Levine, Editor Toussaint Fancher · Last Word on Sports Thu, November 5, 2026 at 2:00 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads After taking care of business and handing the Los Angeles Chargers their seventh loss of the season, the Rams will look to do the same against the Washington Commanders. Although the Commanders' 2-4-1 record is far from impressive, they remain a dangerous team that can win on any given Sunday. Commanders head coach Dan Quinn is currently fighting for his job , and injuries have plagued the team throughout a disappointing season. Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels has missed several games this season after aggravating a previous arm injury, while several other key players have been sidelined for significant periods of time. While they are 2-4-1, the Commanders still have an opportunity to win the weak NFC East. The Commanders just won their second game of the season after defeating the Philadelphia Eagles and currently sit third in the division. This season, the Commanders are 17th in points per game and 26th in points allowed. They have also struggled on third down, converting just 32% of their attempts, while their defense has surrendered too many points. Although the Commanders have been one of the worst teams this season, they have found success running the ball. Led by their dual-threat quarterback, they average 127 rushing yards per game and protect the ball with only three turnovers. The Commanders' biggest weakness lies in their passing defense, which ranks 27th in the league, allowing 243 yards per game and an opponent passer rating of 100.6. The Rams' success largely depends on quarterback Matthew Stafford's ability to effectively move the ball. Stafford is reportedly dealing with soreness in his right arm. He left the locker room after the Chargers game with a bag of ice on his right elbow. This could be a big game for Puka Nacua . Held to only 80 yards in Week 9, Nacua might have over 100 receiving yards this week. The Rams should still find success running the ball, but the overall game will depend on Stafford's effectiveness passing the ball. In a must-win game for the Rams, this news comes at the worst time. Garrett's 21-day practice window is now open, giving him time to ramp up and prepare before he plays again. However, Garrett's return to practice doesn't guarantee his availability for this week's game. "I think just taking it a day at a time is going to be the best way that we can approach it," McVay said. "Think that's the right thing for him, and really just to see how he responds . But I think it's a real positive that we're starting his clock." Tight end Terrance Ferguson will also return to practice this week after sustaining an ankle sprain against the Denver Broncos in Week 3. McVay said it's likely that they will start his 21-day clock, but want to see how he's feeling. Cornerback Jaylen Watson aggravated his shoulder again and will take things day-to-day. Watson dislocated his right shoulder in Week 4 and missed the following game before he returned. Tight end Colby Parkinson missed the last game with a rib injury and is reportedly "making really good progress." This is the first time the Rams have had the opportunity to change the trajectory of their season. They must stick to their plan and execute to keep their winning streak alive. Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton It is early to call the Rams’ game in Maryland Sunday against the Commanders an elimination game, but it sure has the feel of one. Los Angeles is 4-4 and outside the playoff picture currently while the Commanders are 2-4-1 and clinging to life only because the NFC East is so bad. Both teams carry a little momentum into the game. Washington takes the field following their most impressive outing of the season last weekend against Philadelphia while the Rams have won their last two games. The Rams’ latest victory was a 24-9 win over the Chargers in which their offense started extremely slowly, failing to record a first down until late in the second quarter and falling behind 9-3 in the process. Kyren Williams’ one-yard touchdown gave Los Angeles a 10-9 halftime lead. Blake Corum then broke off a 23-yard touchdown run and Matthew Stafford hit Puka Nacua for an 18-yard score in the third quarter. Stafford finished 17-of-25 for 157 yards, one touchdown and one interception, Nacua caught 11 passes for 80 yards and a score, and the Rams rushed for 129 yards while their defense intercepted Justin Herbert twice and kept the Chargers out of the end zone. The Commanders are coming off a much-needed 27-10 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles, their first win in more than a month. Washington fell behind 10-0 during a penalty-filled first quarter before scoring the game’s final 27 points and shutting Philadelphia out over the final three quarters. Jayden Daniels completed 16 of 29 passes for 217 yards, a touchdown and no interceptions, connecting with Stefon Diggs for an eight-yard score, while Rachaad White ran 11 times for 55 yards and the clinching touchdown. Washington finished with 135 yards rushing, but its defense was the bigger story, sacking Tanner McKee five times, intercepting him once and limiting Saquon Barkley to just 30 yards on 13 carries. That showing by the Washington defense sets up the primary storyline for Sunday’s game: the Commanders’ resurgent pass rush against Stafford. The other of course relates to Daniels and his ability to attack a banged-up Rams’ secondary. Historically, Washington has had the upper hand in the series, holding a 24-13-1 regular season record against the Rams, but recent meetings have been much more balanced. Washington has split its past four matchups with Los Angeles dating to 2015, and Sunday’s game will be the Rams’ first trip to Washington since 2020, when Los Angeles won 30-10 in the game that marked Alex Smith’s remarkable return to action following multiple leg surgeries and a long rehab. Rams coach Sean McVay spent seven seasons in Washington’s organization and three as its offensive coordinator before taking the Rams’ job. Let’s dive further into the numbers and see if we can’t find an additional sweat or two. away.headline: Rams-Commanders injury report: McDuffie, Curl miss 2nd straight practice
away.blurb: The Los Angeles Rams took the field for their second practice of the week on Thursday, and none of the injury concerns from Wednesday have subsided. There were only two changes from Day 1 to 2: Steve Avila was upgraded from limited to full, and Grant Stuard was downgraded from limited to DNP. Joe Cardona remains out with an ankle injury, too, so it's unclear if he'll be able to play on Sunday after missing last week's game. Myles Garrett and Terrance Ferguson were limited for the second day in a row. They'll have one more practice before being given a final game status for Sunday. On the Commanders ' side, Treylon Burks missed his second straight practice, and Dyami Brown was added to Thursday's report with a calf injury that caused him to be listed as limited. Sam Cosmi was limited for the second day in a row, too. As for Trent McDuffie, Kam Curl and Colby Parkinson, their statuses haven't changed. They all missed their second straight practice, remaining on the sidelines Thursday. McDuffie is dealing with a back injury, while Parkinson has an issue with his ribs and Curl has a foot injury. away.headline: Rams Injury Report: Myles Garrett Returns, But Bad News Continues to Pile Up
away.blurb: While the Los Angeles Rams got some good injury news on Wednesday, the injuries also continue to pile up. Both Myles Garrett and Terrance Ferguson opened their practice windows as they work to return from injured reserve. However, cornerback Jaylen Watson’s season is over with a shoulder injury and cornerback Trent McDuffie was a non-participant with a back injury. The biggest knock for the Rams is Watson being placed on injured reserve and being out for the season. Watson was the team’s top free agent signing as the Rams looked to rebuild their cornerback room this offseason. After missing Week 4 with a dislocated shoulder, Watson reaggravated the injury in the third quarter of the team’s win against the Chargers. “The likelihood of it coming out and doing further damage to it is a very high probability. You could strap it, but it would restrict his movement,” said head coach Sean McVay. “Just some of the different things that we've received from our doctors, it's the right thing to do by him, even though it sucks because he's been such a bright spot for us.” “It's exciting. It's great to be able to get him back out there,” said McVay. “He'll probably take half the reps today. If you have 30 reps, he'll take 15 and then we'll see how he feels coming out of that. Hopefully, it's just a little bit of an increase incrementally at a time.” In addition to Garrett being back, Ferguson and running back Ronnie Rivers returned to practice as well. Ferguson should provide some insurance if Parkinson can’t play for a second straight week, while Rivers could be helpful on special teams. Also limited were linebacker Grant Stuard (hamstring), left guard Steve Avila (hamstring), and wide receiver Jordan Whittington (back). Coming out of the Chargers game, one of the big stories was Matthew Stafford being seen walking out of the locker room with ice around his right arm . Stafford showed up as a full participant on Wednesday’s injury report with a right elbow injury. home.headline: Rams-Commanders injury report: McDuffie, Curl miss 2nd straight practice
home.blurb: The Los Angeles Rams took the field for their second practice of the week on Thursday, and none of the injury concerns from Wednesday have subsided. There were only two changes from Day 1 to 2: Steve Avila was upgraded from limited to full, and Grant Stuard was downgraded from limited to DNP. Joe Cardona remains out with an ankle injury, too, so it's unclear if he'll be able to play on Sunday after missing last week's game. Myles Garrett and Terrance Ferguson were limited for the second day in a row. They'll have one more practice before being given a final game status for Sunday. On the Commanders ' side, Treylon Burks missed his second straight practice, and Dyami Brown was added to Thursday's report with a calf injury that caused him to be listed as limited. Sam Cosmi was limited for the second day in a row, too. As for Trent McDuffie, Kam Curl and Colby Parkinson, their statuses haven't changed. They all missed their second straight practice, remaining on the sidelines Thursday. McDuffie is dealing with a back injury, while Parkinson has an issue with his ribs and Curl has a foot injury. home.headline: Commanders' final injury report takes a serious turn along defensive line
home.blurb: Javon Kinlaw missed practice all week, so it wasn't much of a surprise when the Washington Commanders officially listed him as out on their final injury report Friday. The surprise was Daron Payne , who was added with a foot injury; he's officially questionable after being limited in practice on the last day. John Bates, Treylon Burks, and Jer’Zhan Newton were all also listed as questionable for Sunday night's game against Philadelphia. Newton is still in his 21-day practice window as he returns from a pectoral injury ; the Commanders must still activate him before he's eligible. Bates improved from not practicing at all to limited, while Burks went from limited to not practicing , then back to limited on Friday . Commanders head coach Dan Quinn didn't hide how impressed he was with Newton's recovery work Wednesday: "Man, he has worked his ass off." Luke McCaffrey, Charles Omenihu , and Deatrich Wise Jr. were limited Friday but carried no game designation; Omenihu was limited all week with groin/ankle injuries. Nick Allegretti rebounded from missing Thursday's practice by returning as a full participant Friday. Jayden Daniels, Stefon Diggs, and Marcus Mariota all finished the week as full participants and carry no game designation. Philadelphia has its own injury problems , ruling out five players for Sunday night's game, including receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring), Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad), Britain Covey (knee), Jonathan Jones (hamstring), and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle). Cornerback Jakorian Bennett is questionable with a knee injury, while Saquon Barkley was limited Friday with hamstring/back issues but carries no game designation. Jalyx Hunt (knee/ankle) and Moro Ojomo (neck) were also limited but have no game designation. Commanders News: Treylon Burks Misses Practice With McLaurin Out Before Eagles Rematch | Burgundy Roundup UPDATE: Friday evening brought worse news. Tashan Reed of The Washington Post reported that Payne suffered a significant foot injury during practice and will miss Sunday's game. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo also reported that Payne could be headed to injured reserve, with further testing expected Saturday. home.headline: Commanders-Rams Injury Report Raises New Concern on Depleted Defensive Line
home.blurb: The Washington Commanders released their first Week 9 injury report as the team gears up for its matchup with the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday. Jer'Zhan (Johnny) Newton practiced fully on Wednesday after being limited throughout last week. A day after the team placed both starting defensive tackles on injured reserve , Shy Tuttle was limited with a shoulder injury. Newton returned to practice last week as the team opened his 21-day practice window while he recovers from a torn pectoral muscle. He was downgraded to OUT before the Eagles game, but Commanders head coach Dan Quinn likes how his return is progressing. "The arrow is going up for sure, and I'm very optimistic for it. But it's important to stack another good week of him in practice and movements." Newton must still be activated from injured reserve before he can play against Los Angeles. Treylon Burks was another name missing from Wednesday's practice, as the receiver continues dealing with the foot injury that left him questionable against Philadelphia . He played anyway and led Washington with 81 receiving yards on three catches, including a 53-yard gain. With Terry McLaurin out for the season, the Commanders need Burks available, but missing Wednesday's practice doesn't necessarily mean he'll be unavailable against Los Angeles. Stefon Diggs also sat out Wednesday, although his absence was listed as rest rather than an injury. John Bates (shoulder) and Sam Cosmi (knee) were limited, while Jayden Daniels (left elbow) and Colson Yankoff (knee) practiced fully. Thursday's injury report should provide a clearer picture of where Burks and Tuttle stand heading into the weekend. However, two straight wins have put the Rams right back in the thick of the playoff race. With two road games coming up against the Washington Commanders and Arizona Cardinals, Los Angeles received some promising news. Getting Ferguson back should help the offense as well. The unit has been inconsistent at times, but it has improved in the last two wins. With star receiver Davante Adams on the shelf, and Puka Nacua routinely battling some ailment, having Ferguson team up with veteran Tyler Higbee will only help signal caller Matthew Stafford. With wins over the Commanders and the Cardinals over the next two weeks, the Rams could truly be back in contention. picks.blurb: 3 Bold Predictions for Panthers in Season-Defining Matchup with Broncos - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football TNF: Jaguars-Ravens preview Wemby makes NBA history Ronaldo retires from Portugal Luka gets fan booted First CFP rankings 3 Bold Predictions for Panthers in Season-Defining Matchup with Broncos Green Bay Packers place kicker Trey Smack (28) reacts after missing a point-after-touchdown attempt against the Carolina Panthers Tork Mason/Green Bay Press-Gazette | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Zach Roberts · Carolina Panthers On SI Thu, November 5, 2026 at 7:00 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Carolina Panthers have fallen to 3-4 after a really inspiring 3-2 start. Losing two games in a row in a demoralizing fashion, at least on the offensive side of the ball, is crushing, but it's especially bad when the schedule has no reprieve. The Panthers have to turn it around. Unfortunately, they've got the AFC West-leading Denver Broncos coming to town. The Panthers are underdogs , and no one's picking them to win. It could be another ugly one. But in the spirit of success, here are some bold predictions for the contest. Bryce Young is sacked less than twice Carolina Panthers quarterback Bryce Young (9) tries to avoid pressure from Green Bay Packers defensive end Brenton Cox Jr. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Being sacked twice in a game doesn't feel like a bold prediction. But Bryce Young has been sacked 11 times in the last two games. Getting back down to a normal number of sacks feels like an impossible task for everyone involved, especially the offensive line that can't seem to hold up for even two seconds. The offensive line could look different (and should). Young's knee should be healthier, so he can get back to evading pressure as he did in the early going. And Brad Idzik should have enough data to call plays to help offset the porous line. Young's health, a better line, and smarter planning should help the sacks and pressure regress to the mean. Bo Nix passes for less than 200 yards You'd be forgiven for checking the Panthers' depth chart and not knowing who the cornerbacks were. For an offense (Denver's) that has struggled to throw the ball down the field, Carolina's secondary has to feel like a gift from above. But Marco Wilson was solid in his debut, and the Panthers should get Jaelan Phillips back. Nix hasn't challenged anyone down the field all year, and we don't expect that to start. That's the recipe for success, especially for a defense that wants to get downhill more with a new coordinator. Tetairoa McMillan returns to form Carolina Panthers wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan (4) during warmups prior to the game against the Green Bay Packers | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect There's a temptation to expect Tetairoa McMillan to see Pat Surtain more often than not and produce like he did against the Cleveland Browns, when the defense put its best corner on him and sent pressure. Why shouldn't the Browns repeat that? Well, they might, but as mentioned, the game plan should be better to offset that. And with Jalen Coker healthy, the Broncos won't be able to necessarily shade McMillan with Surtain 100% of the time. So, he should be able to bounce back. Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton The Denver Broncos (6-2) head to Charlotte on Sunday looking to strengthen their hold on first place in the AFC West when they face the Carolina Panthers (3-4) at Bank of America Stadium. Although their record is a game below .500, the Panthers are also a first place team as they sit atop the NFC South. The Broncos have won four straight since a loss in early October at San Francisco. Carolina has suffered lopsided defeats in each of their last two games. This past Sunday, Bo Nix and the Broncos staged an impressive comeback to beat Kansas City, 28-24. Denver trailed 24-13 in the fourth quarter before Nix found Nate Adkins for a touchdown and Jaylen Waddle for the two-point conversion. After a missed Chiefs’ field goal, Nix connected with rookie Jonah Coleman for 51 yards, setting up Coleman’s go-ahead five-yard touchdown with 1:56 remaining. Denver then preserved the victory when its defense stopped Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs on fourth-and-goal. Nix finished 20-of-32 for 222 yards and two touchdowns. Denver has now won 15 one-score games over the past two seasons. As mentioned, Carolina has lost two straight, most recently losing at Green Bay last Thursday 27-19. The Panthers actually led 10-6 early in the second quarter behind a Chuba Hubbard touchdown, but Green Bay answered with 21 straight points to take control. Bryce Young completed 23 of 41 passes for 209 yards, one touchdown and one interception, while Hubbard supplied 81 yards and a touchdown on 22 carries plus seven catches for 38 yards. Carolina made things interesting when Young hit Jalen Coker for a 26-yard touchdown with 5:37 left, but the Panthers failed on the two-point conversion and never scored again. The most troubling stats to emerge from the game was Young being sacked six times and Carolina’s offense managing only 258 yards. The central storyline is therefore strength against vulnerability: a Carolina offensive line that surrendered six sacks at Green Bay now has to protect Young against Denver, while the Panthers must find a way to slow a Broncos team that has developed a remarkable habit of winning tight games. Recent history strongly favors Denver. The Broncos hold a 7-2 all-time advantage over Carolina, including the postseason, and won the teams’ most recent meeting 28-14 in Denver on October 27, 2024. That game featured the same starting quarterbacks expected Sunday: Nix shredded Carolina for 284 yards and three touchdown passes, added a rushing touchdown and posted a 124.2 passer rating, while Young threw for 224 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions. away.headline: Broncos' Week 9 injury report: WR Pat Bryant gearing up for return
away.blurb: After missing the last four games with an ankle injury, the Denver Broncos designated wide receiver Pat Bryant to return from injured reserve, opening his window to be activated to the 53-man roster. WR Courtland Sutton, meanwhile, was considered limited as he enjoyed a veteran rest day. Ditto for defensive end Zach Allen. Both will play against the Panthers. What's less certain is the Week 9 status of four key defensive players in safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle), safety Brandon Jones (hamstring), defensive lineman Eyioma Uwazurike (shoulder), and cornerback Kris Abrams-Draine (ankle) — all of whom did not practice on Wednesday. Jones, Abrams-Draine, and Uwazurike were injured in Week 8 and their status for Sunday's contest is to be determined. They'd need to get in at least a few limited practices on Thursday and Friday to increase their chances of suiting up. Hufanga has been sidelined since Oct. 11 — he was initially expected to miss 2-3 games — and could be held out once more with Denver's Week 10 bye looming. This article was originally published on www.si.com/nfl/broncos/onsi as Broncos' Week 9 Injury Report: WR Pat Bryant Gearing Up for Return . That will likely happen sooner rather than later as Bryant was marked as a full practice participant on the team's first Week 9 injury report ahead of Sunday's road game at Carolina . Bryant was carted off the field amid Denver's Week 4 loss against the 49ers with what appeared to be a significant injury, though the second-year wideout avoided being placed on short-term injured reserve. Also listed as a full participant was Bryant's fellow pass-catcher, WR Jaylen Waddle, who's still nursing a minor chest issue. Waddle looked no worse for wear in last week's comeback victory over Kansas City , snagging three passes for 39 yards and a touchdown. A Potential Boost to Denver's Passing Offense Finally, the Broncos — if they choose to activate him this week — could be back at full strength in their receiving corps, with Waddle, Sutton, Bryant, Marvin Mims, and Troy Franklin all sharing the same field together. Bryant totaled nine receptions for 133 yards and a touchdown prior to going down, with his lone score coming in Denver's Week 3 upset of the Los Angeles Rams. He also snagged a two-point conversion earlier in the season. With sure hands and a wide catch radius, Bryant will again provide quarterback Bo Nix a security blanket over the middle of the field and in the red zone, helping to boost a passing offense that currently ranks 25th in the NFL, averaging 180.4 yards per game through the air. away.blurb: Injury Report: CB Pat Surtain II not assigned game status, 4 Broncos listed as questionable for Week 8 game vs. Chiefs Skip to main content Primary nav Game Day ENGLEWOOD, Colo. — Cornerback Pat Surtain II appears poised to return to the field for the Broncos. Surtain (ankle) was a full participant for the third consecutive practice, and he was not assigned a game status for Sunday's matchup against the Chiefs. The absence of a game status indicates Surtain will be available to play. While Surtain is expected to make his return, four Broncos are listed as questionable to play in Sunday's game. Defensive lineman Zach Allen (hamstring), tackle Garett Bolles (hip), safety Brandon Jones (hamstring) and wide receiver Jaylen Waddle (chest) are questionable for the division matchup. All four players were limited in Friday's practice. Running back RJ Harvey (knee) — who was added the Broncos' injury report on Thursday — and safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) were both ruled out. Harvey did not practice on Friday after he was limited on Thursday. Hufanga (ankle) was listed as a limited participant on Thursday. Wide receiver Pat Bryant was a full participant in his return to practice on Wednesday. The Broncos' All-Pro cornerback suffered his injury against the 49ers in Week 4. Wide receiver Marvin Mims Jr. (ankle), inside linebacker Karene Reid (elbow) and defensive tackle Malcolm Roach (neck) were all full participants on Friday and also not assigned game statuses. away.blurb: Allen went down in the fourth quarter of last Sunday's 30-16 win over the Arizona Cardinals and appeared to be favoring his right hamstring. He was able to walk off the field into the team's blue medical tent, but did not return to the game. Allen finished the game standing on the sideline without his helmet as Denver closed out a win. After the game, Allen was asked about the injury and said, "Yeah, I'll be fine. Yeah, I'll be good." He was listed as questionable for today's game on Friday's injury report. Allen (and all of the players listed as questionable) are active and set to play against the Chiefs today. Denver Broncos defensive lineman Zach Allen ( hamstring ) is active for Sunday's game against the Kansas City Chiefs. Allen has been one of the best interior defensive linemen in the NFL this season, totaling 24 tackles, 19 quarterback hits, 4.5 sacks, two pass breakups and one forced fumble through seven games. He's well on his way toward earning another first-team All-Pro nod after securing the first such honor of his career last season. The Broncos ' defensive line rotation this season has been led by Allen ( 343 snaps ), Malcolm Roach ( 283 ), Eyioma Uwazurike ( 272 ) and D.J. Jones ( 220 ). home.headline: 7 Injuries to Monitor for Panthers: Good News on the Horizon?
home.blurb: The Carolina Panthers have arguably been the most injured team all season. They've lost four cornerbacks, their top two edge rushers, both starting tackles, a starting guard, the second running back, the third wide receiver, their prized rookie wide receiver, and more. Those players are all out right now. On Tuesday, Xavier Legette and Jonathon Brooks both got some work in on the side. So did Mike Jackson. The Panthers reportedly plan to open the 21-day return window for Brooks and Legette sooner rather than later. Joe Person reported that Jaelan Phillips and Jaycee Horn were also working off to the side. Horn hasn't played since Week 3, and Phillips has been out the last couple of weeks. The Panthers officially opened the 21-day return window for Brady Christensen. They want him to get his feet under him first, but he could potentially be in the lineup sooner rather than later. At times, they've been without Devin Lloyd, Bobby Okereke, Jalen Coker, Monroe Freeling, Bobby Brown, and Pat Jones. It has been a bloodbath, and one could reasonably argue that it has played a hand in their 3-4 record. After a "mini-bye," so to speak, the Panthers are back in action this week ahead of an important matchup with the Denver Broncos . And fortunately, there are some positive rumblings in the injury world for once. Panthers are beginning to get some good injury news Through seven contests, the Panthers have honestly dropped like flies. Starting in Week 3, it seems like every single game costs a player a trip to the IR or at least a couple of games on the bench, unable to suit up. That didn't end last week, with Will Lee III going down. He may avoid the IR, but he probably won't play this week. It's just been that kind of season, which is a shame given the talent this roster actually has when it's healthy. Regardless, though, things may be beginning to turn in Carolina's favor. There are several injuries to monitor this week, and there is plenty of good news that seems to be on the horizon. And perhaps the best update of all: Bryce Young hasn't missed any snaps, but he has clearly been hobbled by a knee injury, sapping his mobility. Young said he's "good," although he has never said it's been a problem. Dave Canales said it was hampering his quarterback, and on Tuesday, the coach said Young was "ready to rock," and reports suggest that Young's mobility is much improved. home.headline: Injuries beginning to take their toll on the Panthers' secondary, offensive line
home.source: The Associated Press- Sports on MSN
home.blurb: “Just wanna see the guys connected,” Panthers coach Dave Canales said. "I just wanna see them excited about going out there and executing the plan. And playing fast, playing the physical brand. And the effort’s been there. Those things are right. But I know that we can make strides with being able to get everybody on the same page, tying in the whole unit.” Moton, the team's longtime right tackle, was able to return to action three weeks ago, but since injured his fibula and has been placed on injured reserve. Ekwonu is expected back in the next month or so. CHARLOTTE, N.C. (AP) — The Carolina Panthers are probably wishing they could petition the NFL for another bye week. Mounting injuries to the secondary and offensive line have begun to take their toll on the Panthers (3-4), who have dropped two straight games and fallen into a tie with the Atlanta Falcons for first place in the NFC South. On Friday, the Panthers fired defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero after the team allowed Jordan Love to throw for 288 yards and three touchdowns in a 27-19 loss to the Green Bay Packers. Carolina entered the game last in the league in run defense. The Panthers promoted defensive line coach Todd Wash as interim defensive coordinator. Evero's fate may have been sealed when starting cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson went down in a Week 3 loss to the Cleveland Browns and were placed on injured reserve. Since then, the two cornerbacks who were replaced Horn and Jackson have suffered injuries. Akayleb Evans was placed on IR last week and Will Lee injured his hamstring against the Packers in the first half and had to leave the game. Canales said the injuries were taken into account when he fired Evero, but added that the decision was based on the big picture and “a lot of information." Things are just as shaky on the offensive line where the Panthers are playing without three starters, including tackles Taylor Moton and Ickey Ekwonu and guard Damien Lewis. Bryce Young was under constant pressure against the Packers. He was hurried 22 times, hit nine times and sacked six times. “We’ve got to make sure we do a good job of giving him solutions when they do have overloaded pressures and zero looks and things," Canales said. "But it wasn’t just that. They got after us with some four-man rushes and some stunts that we didn’t pass off well. That created a little bit of pressure there as well.” Rookie first-round pick Monroe Freeling has struggled at right tackle this season. Running back Chuba Hubbard continues to be a bright spot for the Panthers despite playing behind an offensive line that has struggled to open holes. Hubbard was used extensively against the Packers and gained 81 yards on 22 carries while hauling in a team-high seven passes for 38 yards. He's clearly the only back offensive coordinator Brad Idzik trusts at this point in the season. home.headline: Both Broncos starting safeties in danger of missing Panthers game after practice injury update
home.blurb: According to the Broncos' official injury report, Hufanga remains sidelined by an ankle injury , while Jones is dealing with a hamstring issue. Neither player has been ruled out, but their availability remains uncertain. Hufanga has missed Denver's last three games since suffering his injury against the Los Angeles Chargers. The Broncos have already needed to make adjustments in the secondary while waiting for his return. Jones, meanwhile, entered the previous matchup against Kansas City with a questionable designation because of his hamstring. His potential absence would leave Denver facing another significant adjustment in the defensive backfield. The injury concerns extend beyond the safety position. Cornerback Kris Abrams-Draine missed Wednesday's practice with an ankle injury, while defensive lineman Eyioma Uwazurike sat out because of a shoulder issue. Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton Two of the league’s bigger disappointments meet Sunday afternoon at SoFi Stadium when the Chargers (0-7) host the Texans (2-5). Los Angeles is the only team in the NFL without a win and are as a result, firmly entrenched in the cellar in the AFC West. Houston sits in second in the AFC South but are three games behind the first place Jaguars. The Texans take the field following their bye week. They were last in action on October 25 when they lost a disappointing 27-21game in overtime at home to the New York Giants. Houston rallied from a seven-point fourth-quarter deficit to force overtime on C.J. Stroud’s 3-yard touchdown pass to Xavier Hutchinson with 52 seconds remaining. Stroud finished 17-of-28 for a season-low 153 yards and two touchdowns, while Woody Marks ran 19 times for 66 yards, but Houston produced only 237 total yards. The glaring issue was on defense. The Texans surrendered a season-high 188 rushing yards, including 124 and a touchdown to Cam Skattebo . The Chargers’ search for their first victory continues following their most recent game, a 24-9 loss last Sunday to the Rams. The Chargers had a 9-3 lead late in the first half but went scoreless over the final 38 minutes of the game. Justin Herbert completed 24 of 32 passes for 257 yards, but threw two interceptions, and the Chargers failed to reach the end zone for the second consecutive game. Los Angeles managed just 64 yards rushing with all nine Chargers’ points coming on Cameron Dicker field goals. The Chargers hold a narrow 6-5 advantage in the all-time series, but Houston has won the last two meetings, including two especially consequential victories. The Texans routed Los Angeles 32-12 in the AFC Wild Card round following the 2024 season, intercepting Herbert four times as Houston erased an early 6-0 deficit and ran away with the game. Houston then went back to SoFi Stadium in Week 17 last season and beat the Chargers 20-16, giving the Texans consecutive victories in the series for the first time. The Los Angeles Chargers are 0-7 after falling to the Los Angeles Rams on the road in Week 8. Now the Chargers will have a chance to face off against the Houston Texans at home in Week 9. The Texans have found their fair share of struggles this season at 2-5, but they are fresh off of their annual bye and are well-rested for the matchup. The Bolts entered this week as 4.5-point underdogs, per FanDuel Sportsbook . The over/under is currently set at 41.5 points. The Chargers struggled once again when facing the Rams. The Chargers had a 9-3 lead with 2 minutes to go in the second quarter, but they proceeded to give up a touchdown drive to close out the first half, which gave the Rams the lead going into the locker room. From there, the Rams capitalized and scored twice more in the third quarter to take a 24-9 lead, which ended up being the final score. Hope is not lost for the Chargers as they hold on to the No. 1 overall pick for the 2027 NFL Draft. However, getting a win or two would give them some morale for the second half of the season. Perhaps this will be the week the Chargers will have a chance to get their first win. away.headline: Texans Need to Trade for RB After David Montgomery Injury Update
away.blurb: According to Ryans after the Texans' first practice of the week before facing the LA Chargers, Montgomery has already been ruled out for this weekend as he continues to rehab from his lingering groin injury he's been working back from since Week 5 . Montgomery will continue to be listed as week-to-week, but there's still no exact date to circle just yet for when the Texans' lead running back will return to the lineup. And with that mysterious timeline in mind, perhaps there's a case to be made for the Texans to go out and trade for another running back before the NFL trade deadline arrives early next week. This is one of the final moments of the season in which the front office can go out to add an immediate upgrade to their roster before taking on the second half of their schedule (and the postseason), and being without a stable ground game will only hurt the Texans' offense long-term. Adding one more reliable ball carrier into the room could add some much-needed security and stability on the ground, while also providing a backup plan in case Montgomery is at all limited after recovering from his lengthy groin injury absence. home.headline: Chargers have major decisions looming with crowded injured reserve list
home.blurb: As things stand, the Bolts have eight players on injured reserve , with only one out for the entire season (center Tyler Biadasz). Things aren’t getting any better soon on that front, as the Chargers may put Derwin James on the IR with a hamstring injury. Outside of Biadasz, only seven players could return for the season. Rashawn Slater's absence is the most detrimental. The Chargers' offensive line entered the season with some major question marks, and that unit remains among the most worrisome. Perryman has yet to play this season after playing 10 games in 2025. The Chargers veteran linebacker is currently on the IR with an undisclosed injury, but he is nearing a return. As for Keandre Lambert-Smith, Branson Taylor and Scott Matlock; all three were designated players to return from IR. picks.blurb: Experts Don't Like Patriots Chance to Defeat Packers in Week 9 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football TNF: Jaguars-Ravens preview Wemby makes NBA history Ronaldo retires from Portugal Luka gets fan booted First CFP rankings Experts Don't Like Patriots Chance to Defeat Packers in Week 9 (Rich Storry-Imagn Images) Matt Levine · Roundtable Sports Thu, November 5, 2026 at 9:30 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New England Patriots were able to take down the Miami Dolphins last week, improving their record to 5-3 on the season. New England didn't play the prettiest game on the field, but at this point for them, a win is a win. With all the injuries that the Patriots have seen take place, especially to the offense, the team has been able to stay alive. This week, the Patriots will be hosting the Green Bay Packers, giving the team a real challenge on its hands. Green Bay, like New England, has started to play much better of late, finally put things together on the field. The Packers will be entering the game with a record of 5-3, with both sides of the ball clicking for the team. New England is going to have to be careful in this game; otherwise, they could be on the losing end of the contest. Analysts Gary Davenport, Brad Gagnon, Kris Knox, Moe Moton, Brent Sobleski, Wes O'Donnell, and Ian Hanford of Bleacher Report all made picks for the game between the two teams. But six of the seven experts went with Green Bay to take down the Patriots in this matchup. Only Gagnon went with New England to win the game, despite this contest being played at home for the Patriots. But the Packers recent play likely has to do with how confident those around the league are heading into the week. One key for New England this week will be how quarterback Drake Maye performs, especially when it comes to turnovers. The Green Bay defense can be feisty at times, using its opportunistic nature to get the best of opposing quarterbacks. Maye will have to find a way to overcome the injuries that the Patriots have seen this year, going against this tough defense. But the veteran quarterback has done well this year , even with his issues earlier in the season. Against Green Bay, the Patriots may need to rely on the running game a little more, taking some pressure off Maye's shoulders. Head coach Mike Vrabel will have to put his signal-caller into a strong position to win, avoiding any issues. The offensive line will also need to hold up in the game, giving Maye time to throw the ball against this defensive front. Kickoff for the Patriots game against the Packers is scheduled to take place at 1:25 p.m. PT/4:25 p.m. ET at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough.

picks.headline: NFL straight-up picks, Week 9: Packers-Patriots has us torn in otherwise chalky week
picks.blurb: The Thursday Night Football matchup pits a surging Jacksonville Jaguars team against a Baltimore Ravens squad forced to start an undrafted rookie at quarterback. The early slate Sunday includes a backup extravaganza between the New York Giants and Philadelphia Eagles as well as mismatches like Jets-Chiefs and Lions-Dolphins. But 4:30 p.m. Eastern? That's when we get to see which erstwhile contender might be for real when the Green Bay Packers face the New England Patriots. Sunday night brings the new-look Chicago Bears against a Tampa Bay Buccaneers team that didn't need to complete a single pass last week (OK, a bit of a stretch but should still be fun). And on Monday, Josh Allen takes on the league's best, most aggressive defense. That's made Week 9 a bit easier to predict, but it's not chalk across the board on our end. Welcome back to For The Win's straight-up, moneyline NFL picks column. I ended 2023 as Pickwatch’s top expert in a field of hundreds. The two seasons that followed? Ehhhhh, we don't like to talk about that. But I'm back and hopeful I'll either be good enough to rejoin the top 25 or, barring that, be so destructively bad you're left with no choice but to fade my picks all the way to prosperity. Joining me for 2026 is a six-person panel ranging from FTW editors (Charles Curtis, Wajih AlBaroudi and Jeff Smith) to betting analysts (Prince Grimes) to NFL writers (Robert Zeglinski, who is THRIVING this year, and Andrew Joseph). Here are our Week 9 picks. Jaguars at Ravens Bengals at Falcons Browns at Saints Cowboys at Colts Broncos at Panthers Lions at Dolphins Giants at Eagles Jets at Chiefs Rams at Commanders Texans at Chargers Cardinals at Seahawks Packers at Patriots Raiders at 49ers Buccaneers at Bears Bills at Vikings Season to date: Since our editing software occasionally struggles to make these picks super clear, here they are in an easier to read (but impossible to cut and paste) .jpg you can click to expand: Let's break out three games to talk about. Survivor pick of the week: Houston Texans (-4.5) over the Los Angeles Chargers We haven't burned Houston yet in my quest to turn what should be the easiest pick of the week into a coin flip. Now the Texans are coming off a bye and facing the shattered remnants of the Chargers on a home field that will be even more listless than usual in Los Angeles. DeMeco Ryans has a path from 2-5 to 6-5 over the next four weeks (against the Chargers, Browns , Colts and Ravens). He's not going to collapse on the first step. Last week : 1-0 Season to date : 4-4 Hardest favorite to back: New England Patriots (-3) over the Green Bay Packers Tom Brady returns to Foxborough, which Fox would like you to believe is a momentous occasion but isn't the first time he's been back to Gillette Stadium . The bigger story is two 5-3 teams have stabilized after iffy starts and a Drake Maye-Jordan Love shootout could be the best game of the year. Or, the Patriots' injuries could finally sink them back to "pretender" status. Why I like this pick : The Patriots have only lost once at home in the last 58 weeks (to the Buffalo Bills). Maye has been able to make adjustments on the fly, elevating targets like Eli Raridon, Pop Douglas and Kyle Williams the last few weeks with A.J. Brown, Romeo Doubs and Mack Hollins all missing time due to injury. That includes a comeback effort in Week 8, albeit against a bad Miami Dolphins team. The Packers have the same problem many Matt LaFleur teams have had; they struggle to close out games. The run attack is a disaster. No one trusts Trey Smack with an end-of-half field goal at this point, let alone one that could decide a game in the fourth quarter. Why I don't like this pick : New England has yet to play a game without committing a turnover. Green Bay forces them more than all but one other team in the NFL. That leaves a top 10 defense to clean up a Patriot offense potentially missing its top three wideouts, its 1b running back and both its starting guards. The Patriots defense is solid, but not spectacular. Jordan Love is playing the best football of his life, taking shots downfield with incredible touch and accuracy. Granted, far too many of those throws wind up dropped, but that hasn't deterred him from taking risks capable of paying off in a massive way. Last week : 0-2 Season to date : 6-2 Upset pick of the week: Atlanta Falcons (+3) over the Cincinnati Bengals Last week's upset pick failed to account for a monsoon in Tampa. Still, it was worth it just to see Michael Penix Jr. throw more interceptions than the Buccaneers had pass attempts. AND YET, I AM ON THE FALCONS FOR A SECOND STRAIGHT WEEK. Well, let's unpack just how dumb I am. The Bengals keep touching the stove. Cincinnati just gave up 121 yards and two touchdowns to Tony Pollard and now has to face Bijan Robinson. That defense was the backdrop for the biggest game of Cam Ward's career and now has to face an angry Michael Penix Jr. who goes from rainstorms to the cozy confines of Madrid, which... huh actually I don't know how that's gonna affect things. The Falcons have quietly engineered a borderline top 10 defense and have only allowed 11 passing touchdowns this fall. That will place some of the onus on a run game that's underwhelmed behind the average efforts of Chase Brown. The Bengals' best win this season is over... the Buccaneers? The Lamar Jackson-less Ravens? The Dolphins or Titans? Ooooof, that resume. It's the Falcons. Joe Burrow just racked up about 1,000 yards on his own to fend off the Titans last week. The Cincinnati secondary is capable of shutting down a top-heavy receiving corps. It's the Falcons. picks.headline: Packers at Patriots: Predictions, picks and odds for NFL Week 9 game
picks.blurb: The Patriots are likely to be on A.J. Brown watch once again. After the receiver missed Sunday's win over the Dolphins with a knee injury, Mike Vrabel said Monday that the team would need to see how Brown progresses before determinig his status for the upcoming tilt. Micah Parsons is expected to make his much-anticipated return to practice this week for the Packers, but he might still be a long way out from contributing. Matt LaFleur said the edge rusher might need the full 21-day window before being added to the active roster, which would mean a late November return. If there is any change to running back Josh Jacobs' disciplinary status, it won't come from the Packers. LaFleur said this week that the team plans to continue on with the ball carrier as the NFL extends its investigation. Patriots vs Packers odds, moneyline, over/under Opening lines: Spread: Patriots -3.5 Moneyline: Patriots -160; Packers +145 Get the edge with our exclusive NFL betting picks Patriots vs Packers USA TODAY expert picks Adam Kaufman: Patriots 24, Packers 23 The Patriots are 17-0 with Drake Maye when favored by at least a field goal and we just may close there by Sunday afternoon. Who am I to disagree with a great trend? The Packers possess a dynamic passing offense but, even with Josh Jacobs back, still can't run the football with any efficiency. Plus, Christian Watson is dealing with a rib injury that sent him to the hospital for a portion of last week's primetime win over the Panthers. The Pats have the personnel to take advantage defensively, but Maye's offense also has questions around injuries to A.J. Brown, Hunter Henry and others. I'll take New England at home, but I'm expecting nervous pacing around living rooms throughout Massachusetts before this one is settled. Michael Middlehurst-Schwartz: Packers 28, Patriots 27 Bombs away. With a matchup of two daring downfield passers and lackluster run games, both teams could air it out early and often against one another. Between their reliance on Jordan Love connecting on vertical shots and the pass rush picking up the rest of the defense with pressure, Green Bay might be more reliant of the two on igniting big plays. But the Packers' explosiveness shouldn't be doubted, and it could lead the team to its fifth win in six games. Nicholas Brinkerhoff: Packers 26, Patriots 23 Good luck figuring these teams out. At times, Green Bay looks like a bad team. Then it looks like a Super Bowl contender. The same is true of New England, meaning there is a large range of outcomes we could see in Week 9. Will A.J. Brown play for the Patriots? Does it matter? Drop issues have plagued the star receiver and there's no sign of that disappearing anytime soon. On the other side, Christian Watson made 'Thursday Night Football” look like the WWE with his dramatic return. In the end, we'll trust the Packers offense to be the difference. away.headline: Packers get exciting injury update on Micah Parsons: Report
away.blurb: The Green Bay Packers expect superstar pass rusher Micah Parsons to return to practice next week, according to a report from NFL Network insider Ian Rapoport on Thursday. “Micah Parsons is expected to return to practice next week. Obviously short week, was not able to do it this week. Next week he should be on the practice field if all goes well. And that is an excellent thing for the Green Bay Packers,” Rapoport said. “I expect caution as far as when he’s actually on the playing field. They want to make sure everything around his knee is as strong as possible. “They are taking their time, but his return is coming.” The Packers will take the field for a “Thursday Night Football” matchup against the Carolina Panthers later this evening. Parsons’ next opportunity to return to the field for in-game action is a Week 9 matchup against the New England Patriots next Sunday. The Packers have been without their generational pass rusher for the entirety of the season thus far, as he continues to recover from the ACL tear he suffered in Week 15 of Green Bay’s 2025 campaign. Green Bay faces off against the Minnesota Vikings in Week 10 before taking their bye in Week 11. Thursday night’s matchup against the Panthers will kick off at 8:15 p.m. ET.
