away.headline: Is Matthew Golden playing tonight? Injury update for Packers WR
away.blurb: The 23-year-old had originally been listed as "questionable" due to shoulder and foot injuries, but he was able to suit up for his eighth game of the season. Golden logged a "limited" practice session on Wednesday after being listed as a non-participant in both Monday's estimated injury report and Tuesday's actual practice session. Packers coach Matt LaFleur was asked whether Golden would be available Thursday during a news conference on Tuesday, Oct. 27. LaFleur also pointed out that the nature of the short week would lead to most sessions being a walkthrough, so his players wouldn't get "any real reps" in advance of the game. The Green Bay Packers are preparing to take on the Carolina Panthers on " Thursday Night Football " in Week 8, marking the second time they have played an NFC South team on a short week this season. This time around, there are questions about whether the Packers will have one of their top wide receivers, Matthew Golden , at their disposal for the game. Golden is dealing with shoulder and foot injuries that have cast doubt on his availability for Thursday's game against the Packers. Golden has appeared in all seven Packers games so far in 2026. He has enjoyed a breakout season, tallying 36 catches for 540 yards and three touchdowns, though he has committed a league-high six drops. Here's what to know about Golden's status for the Packers' Week 8 game against the Panthers and how Green Bay may replace him if he cannot play. Is Matthew Golden playing tonight? Golden is officially active for the Packers' Week 8 "Thursday Night Football" matchup against the Panthers. Golden playing isn't a major surprise. NFL Media's Ian Rapoport provided a positive update on the second-year receiver during a Thursday, Oct. 29, appearance on "Good Morning Football." "I'm told he's trending towards playing," Rapoport said . "So, there's a good chance for the Packers that Matthew Golden does get on the field today." "I sure hope so," LaFleur responded . "But again, we're still kind of working through it." "We will have a short indie tomorrow, but to move guys around to see how they look," LaFleur said, describing the team's practice procedures. "But certainly hopeful for [Golden]." Who is Matthew Golden's backup? J. Michael Sturdivant is listed as Golden's primary backup on the Packers' official depth chart . The undrafted rookie from Florida has played sparingly through six games, notching three catches for 22 yards, all of which came in Green Bay's Week 3 loss to the Atlanta Falcons. But while Sturdivant is listed as Golden's backup, Savion Williams and Bo Melton have each logged more snaps than the Florida product. As such, those two may be more likely to fill in for Golden across from Christian Watson if the former Texas star can't play. home.headline: Patriots vs. Packers Wednesday injury report: Hunter Henry among four sidelined
home.blurb: While the 21-day return windows opened for wide receiver Mack Hollins and guard Greg Van Roten, the New England Patriots practiced without an offensive captain on Wednesday. Henry injured his foot before halftime last weekend against the Miami Dolphins. After heading to and from the locker room, the tenured tight end tested things out yet was ultimately downgraded to out in the final quarter. His outing spanned eight offensive snaps as well three catches for 30 yards. That sent rookies Eli Raridon and Tanner Arkin up the depth chart along with August waiver claim Cameron Latu. Elsewhere for New England's 53-man roster, illnesses kept Henderson and Barmore away on Wednesday. The running back had been ruled out for the AFC East meeting at Hard Rock Stadium after missing three straight practices last week, while the defensive tackle started and split a sack. As for the No. 1 wide receiver, Brown missed back-to-back sessions before the road trip with a knee issue in addition to the high ankle sprain that landed him on injured reserve in September. picks.blurb: Raiders vs. 49ers bold predictions for NFL Week 9 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football TNF: Jaguars-Ravens preview Wemby makes NBA history Ronaldo retires from Portugal Luka gets fan booted First CFP rankings Raiders vs. 49ers bold predictions for NFL Week 9 Garrett Kerman, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Tue, November 3, 2026 at 5:56 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Las Vegas Raiders arrive at Levi's Stadium with renewed confidence. The San Francisco 49ers arrive with extra rest and something to prove. Las Vegas snapped a four-game losing streak with a 38–33 victory over the Jets, improving to 4–4. San Francisco, meanwhile, returns from its bye at 6–1 after suffering its first defeat, a 29–20 loss to Atlanta. Their November 8 matchup offers a test of whether the Raiders' rebound represents progress or another temporary escape. The opening market favors San Francisco by 10 points, with a total of 51.5. These predictions envision something more explosive than that total suggests: a quarterback showcase, a monster receiving performance and a decisive fourth-quarter separation. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Brock Purdy throws for 350 yards and four touchdowns Dale Zanine-Imagn Images Purdy will deliver his most convincing statistical statement of the season, reaching 350 passing yards and throwing four touchdown passes. That projection starts with a favorable matchup. Las Vegas has surrendered at least 30 points in five consecutive games, allowing opponents to dictate too many possessions. Even Sunday's victory required the Raiders to overcome 33 points from the Jets. Purdy already has 1,748 passing yards and 15 touchdowns through seven games. Before the bye, he threw for 288 yards against Atlanta despite injuries affecting several important offensive contributors. The Raiders should expect Kyle Shanahan to test their coverage communication immediately. Motion, play-action and layered routes can create uncertainty without requiring Purdy to hold the ball for extended periods. My projection anticipates San Francisco attacking through the air even after establishing a lead. Rather than leaning exclusively on clock management, Shanahan will keep exploiting favorable matchups. Brock Bowers produces 150 receiving yards and two touchdowns The Raiders' best answer will come through Brock Bowers, who will turn a difficult road assignment into a dominant individual performance. The prediction is at least 150 receiving yards and two touchdowns, including one reception covering 40 or more yards. That would require Las Vegas to build its passing plan around Bowers rather than waiting for him to emerge naturally within the progression. Quick throws would establish his involvement, while crossing routes and seam opportunities would provide the bigger gains. Kirk Cousins enters the matchup following a three-touchdown performance against the Jets, and his recent play has kept rookie Fernando Mendoza on the sideline. That continuity matters for this prediction. The Raiders can attack with an experienced quarterback rather than simplifying everything around a developmental transition. The projected game script should also create volume. If San Francisco scores early, Las Vegas will need to maintain an aggressive passing approach rather than protect field position. Bowers would become the central answer, particularly on third downs and near the goal line. His production will keep the Raiders competitive longer than expected, even as their defense struggles to match it. The teams combine for 70 points as San Francisco wins 42–28 The final prediction is a shootout that eventually becomes a comfortable 49ers victory. A 42–28 result would produce 70 total points, sailing past the opening 51.5-point total while giving San Francisco a 14-point winning margin. The logic connects the first two bold predictions, Purdy repeatedly punishes defensive breakdowns, while Cousins and Bowers generate enough offense to prevent an early rout. Ultimately, the difference will be possession-to-possession consistency. Las Vegas will manufacture explosive moments, but San Francisco will sustain more scoring drives and turn one late Raiders mistake into the decisive touchdown. The Raiders will show offensive resilience. The 49ers will show why their ceiling remains substantially higher. Vegas (4-4) vs. San Francisco (6-1). The Niners sit atop the NFC West while the Raiders sit third in the AFC West but just a single game out of the final playoff position. The Raiders snapped a four-game losing streak last Sunday rallying for a 38-33 win over the Jets in New York. Kirk Cousins threw for 247 yards and three touchdowns. Brock Bowers caught seven balls including two for touchdowns and Mike Washington Jr. ran for 83 yards. Cousins has been a bit of a revelation for the Raiders playing better than he has in the past couple of years. The veteran has thrown for 2,124 yards including 19 touchdowns against only five interceptions. Somewhat under the radar, the 49ers return from their bye week with a three-game lead in what was billed in the preseason as the best division in the NFL. When last we saw San Francisco, the Niners were on the short end of a 29-20 game against the Falcons. Brock Purdy was an MVP candidate last season and is back in the mix this season having thrown for 1,748 yards including 15 touchdowns and only four interceptions. Christian McCaffrey is having another banner season, rushing for 389 yards and catching Purdy passes for 251 yards. San Francisco is still a MASH unit on defense, but DeForest Buckner is expected to suit up for his first game back with his original team after being acquired last week from the Colts. This rivalry’s history is remarkably close: the 49ers own an 8-7 edge in 15 regular-season meetings. San Francisco has won four of the past five matchups and each of the last two, including a 34-3 rout in 2018 and a memorable 37-34 overtime victory in Las Vegas on Jan. 1, 2023; the Raiders’ most recent victory is not so recent: a 24-13 upset of the 49ers in Oakland in 2014. Sunday’s revival of the rivalry carries considerably more than regional nostalgia: Las Vegas can continue their surprising playoff push and climb above .500 with an upset, while San Francisco has an opportunity to respond to its first loss, protect its unbeaten home record and reinforce its position atop a competitive NFC West. The 49ers are averaging 28.1 points while allowing just 19.9 per game. Las Vegas has been far more volatile, scoring a healthy 27.6 points per game but surrendering 28.8. away.headline: Raiders' Thursday Injury Report Gives Reason for Cautious Optimism
away.blurb: On Wednesday, the official injury report listed defensive tackles Thomas Booker and Folorunso Fatukasi and tight end Ian Thomas as limited participants. Cornerback Darien Porter missed Wednesday's practice with a groin injury he suffered against the Jets. On Thursday, Las Vegas' injury report remained minimal. Porter returned to practice on Thursday, which is good news for the Raiders' young defensive backfield. He was a limited participant, and Thomas was a full participant. Booker did not practice on Thursday. Dont'e Thornton was limited as well. Raiders' Thursday Injury Report Gives Reason for Cautious Optimism Skip to main content SI.COM The Las Vegas Raiders are just a few days away from facing the San Francisco 49ers on the road. Las Vegas went back to work on Thursday, looking to build upon their Week 9 win over the New York Jets. Las Vegas' success this season has largely depended on the quality of the opponent they face. The Raiders have played well enough to beat four of the league's worst teams, but have struggled against the league's elite, which the 49ers are. Still, those four wins are more than the Raiders had all last season, and they are unquestionably better than last season. It may have been against the Jets, but Las Vegas aims to translate its second-half success against New York to this Sunday against the 49ers. After struggling in the third quarter all season, the Raiders' offense exploded against the Jets. In Week 8, Kirk Cousins led the Raiders downfield to score on their first offensive drive after halftime for the first time all season. It was more than impactful, as it led to Las Vegas producing their best third quarter of the season. The Raiders must continue to play well on offense to help their defense. “I think the first play of the second half might have been the throw to Brock [Bowers], and I thought that was a key play in the game and a great call by our coaches, and that whole drive, to finish that drive, it got us right back in the game, which we needed, very important," Cousins said earlier this week. “If you punt and they go down and score, it could be a whole different story. So, it’s very important, and we’ve got to be really strong in the third quarter the rest of the way. And I felt we have continued, last week in the fourth quarter, continuing to play well in the fourth quarter. But it’s a four-quarter game. You’ve got to do it, all four of them.” Throughout the rest of the season, Las Vegas needs the Cousins who showed up in the third and fourth quarters against the Jets to show up in each of their next three games. Moving forward, they will need that version of Cousins and their offense even before the third quarter. Fatukasi was a full participant as well. Based on their injury report, Las Vegas appears to be the healthiest it has been this season, as their Week 1 injury report listed stars Ashton Jeanty and Brock Bowers. The Raiders will likely give rookie cornerback Hezekiah Masses a bigger role

home.headline: 49ers injury updates: Christian Kirk doesn’t practice on Thursday
home.blurb: The San Francisco 49ers injury report is out for Thursday. As usual, Trent Williams returned to practice after a veteran’s day off. Christian McCaffrey participated on a limited basis. McCaffrey didn’t practice Wednesday, but it wasn’t because of a rest day, so it’s good to see McCaffrey return to practice after dealing with a hamstring injury. The only other change from Wednesday was Christian Kirk. The wide receiver was listed as “Did not participate” with a knee injury after being limited on Wednesday. So, the 49ers would essentially be swapping Demarcus Robinson, who was again limited with an ankle injury, for Kirk if he cannot play. General manager John Lynch already said the team would be without wideouts Deebo Samuel (hamstring) and Mike Evans (ribs/Achilles) this Sunday. There’s the “what if” Brandon Aiyuk suits up with the wide receiver depth depleted, but he hasn’t practiced or played with the team in over a calendar year. Aiyuk may have played his fair share of pickup games on the basketball court, but that doesn’t come close to simulating what an NFL game is like. And that’s before you get into, you know, the other Aiyuk stuff.

home.headline: All-Pro WR Brandon Aiyuk Will Return to 49ers: Report
home.blurb: All-Pro WR Brandon Aiyuk Will Return to 49ers: Report Just over a year after cutting off contact with the San Francisco 49ers , NFL All-Pro wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk will return to the team on Friday, according to a report from ESPN's Adam Schefter . 49ers Legend Steve Young Has Strong Words on Brandon Aiyuk's Return Unlock the latest Heavy on 49ers news — direct to your inbox. Well, this could be a little awkward. "Wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk has turned in paperwork to be reinstated, per his agent Drew Rosenhaus," Schefter wrote on his official X account on Wednesday. "Aiyuk, who currently is on San Francisco's Reserve/Left Squad list, will be reporting to the 49ers' training facility Friday afternoon, per Drew Rosenhaus. ‘Brandon is healthy and ready to get back on the field,' Rosenhaus said. Once Brandon Aiyuk officially reports back to the 49ers, the organization's options are to keep him under his current contract, release him or potentially find a trade partner before Tuesday's deadline." Aiyuk hasn't played in over two years, since he suffered a catastrophic knee injury in Week 7 of the 2024 regular season — after the 49ers signed him to a 4-year, $120 million contract extension. The NFL trade deadline is November 10. "The move Brandon Aiyuk could've made months ago to force the 49ers ' hand," NFL Network's Mike Garafolo wrote on his official X account. "Now finally headed to the facility. Kyle Shanahan was asked in September if Aiyuk was an option and he said no. So this will seemingly result in Aiyuk's release." "49ers WR Brandon Aiyuk has filed for reinstatement and is prepared to report to the team's facility on Friday," The 33rd Team's Ari Meirov wrote on his official X account. " Once he does, San Francisco can't turn him away. The options are to keep him, cut him or somehow find a trade." Relationship Between Aiyuk, 49ers Disintegrated When he signed his contract extension, Aiyuk was coming off consecutive 1,000-yard seasons, including his only NFL All-Pro season in 2023, with 75 receptions for 1,342 yards and 7 touchdowns. Through 7 games in 2024, Aiyuk caught 25 passes for 374 yards and no touchdowns before a catastrophic knee injury in Week 7, when He tore his ACL and MCL against the Kansas City Chiefs . After Aiyuk cut off communications with the 49ers early in the 2025 season, the team chose to void the rest of the guaranteed money in Aiyuk's contract — approximately $25 million in salary for 2026. "We don't know what he's physically going to be like," Schefter said in March . "His knee was shredded." 49ers Desperate for Help at Wide Receiver While the 49ers have repeatedly said Aiyuk is no longer welcome on the team — mostly thanks to a series of social media tirades by Aiyuk — the sad part is that they desperately need help at wide receiver after injuries have decimate that position group. home.headline: AWOL NFL star files for bombshell return to 49ers roster... despite active arrest warrant
home.blurb: Even if he is reinstated, however, Aiyuk is unlikely to ever return to the field for the 49ers. According to ESPN, the most likely outcome is San Francisco releasing him. Shanahan was asked Wednesday what his response was to news of Aiyuk's planned return. 'None,' he said. 'I have no expectation. I've kind of moved on with that mentally... nothing has really changed for me.' 'You can't win the race if you crash out,' Aiyuk said about Shanahan, who suffered a broken hand, three broken ribs and a concussion in a crash that nearly cost him his eye. MORE: NFL bad boy Dre Greenlaw handed huge fine for sucker-punching rival Exiled NFL star Brandon Aiyuk has filed paperwork to be reinstated, with the 49ers wide receiver reportedly expected back at the practice facility on Friday. That is despite Aiyuk being the subject of an active arrest warrant in Santa Clara County - where the 49ers' facility is situated - after he was allegedly caught driving at 104mph outside Levi's Stadium earlier this year. Aiyuk has not played an NFL game since tearing knee ligaments in October 2024, with many fearing for his future after a chaotic offseason saw him fail to report for training camp and threaten to tank his career to force an exit from San Francisco. He is on the 49ers' reserve/did not report list but Aiyuk's new agent said Wednesday that the wide receiver is now plotting a comeback. 'Brandon is healthy and ready to get back on the field,' Drew Rosenhaus told ESPN . Both general manager John Lynch and head coach Kyle Shanahan have suggested the wide receiver will not play another game for the 49ers. While the receiver is on the reserve/did not report list, the 49ers do not have to pay Aiyuk or make a spot for him on their roster. San Francisco previously voided $27 million guaranteed in Aiyuk's contract for 2026 after he failed to participate in meetings and other team activities last summer while rehabilitating his knee injury. In fact, Aiyuk has collected only $48.1 million of his four-year, $120 million contract extension. He was due a $24.9 million option bonus on September 1. The 28-year-old has faced significant criticism over his antics and posts on social media in recent months, including crude jokes he made about Shanahan's offseason car crash. Aiyuk had fired agent Ryan Williams during his long-running dispute with the 49ers and was without representation until Rosenhaus said on Monday that he had been hired. The receiver has previously suggested he wants to play alongside his former college teammate Jayden Daniels on the Washington Commanders.

home.headline: Kyle Shanahan refutes Jay Glazer’s Jauan Jennings report, confirms 49ers FaceTime
home.blurb: While that trade didn’t work out, Lynch and the front office are still doing their due diligence ahead of Tuesday’s 1 p.m. PT trade deadline. San Francisco could still use help at receiver, with rookie De’Zhaun Stribling still “probably over a month away,” per Shanahan. “It’s what personnel people do,” Shanahan said. “They look every week to see who you can add week in and week out and it gets bigger as the trade deadline comes. But JJ was someone we knew, so it was someone we wanted to talk to if we went through with that. And they were willing to do it at the time. So we wanted to have a conversation with him knowing the guy. Receiver is something we’re still looking into, and so is every other position.” One former 49ers receiver is expected back in their building Friday for the first time in almost a year, but Brandon Aiyuk won’t be the solution to San Francisco’s injury woes at the position. “There’s no absolutes in life,” coach Kyle Shanahan said Wednesday, all but shooting down any chance of Aiyuk ever suiting up for the 49ers again , despite his application for reinstatement. That doesn’t mean the 49ers aren’t still in search of players who could bolster a receiving corps that may get Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel and Demarcus Robinson back this week but is still undermanned compared to where it was when training camp opened at the start of August. General manager John Lynch arranged one reunion with the trade for defensive tackle DeForest Buckner , and he isn’t the only old friend the 49ers have tried to bring back in the fold. Shanahan confirmed on Wednesday that the 49ers attempted to swing a deal for Jauan Jennings and that the Vikings were amenable to it but, in the end, Jennings said no, thank you. “It wasn’t, like, a definite no at first,” Shanahan said. “But he was like, ‘Man, Kyle, I’m pretty happy. I’m liking stuff.’ When I heard the way he talked and where we’re at, I agreed with him. It was a good conversation and something that was possible, but that’s why it didn’t go down.” Jennings led the 49ers with 643 receiving yards last season and was second to George Kittle with 975 in 2024, but he left for a contract worth up to $13 million with the Vikings. He reportedly envisioned a larger role that hasn’t materialized, with only six catches on 10 targets in six games. But Shanahan clarified that there was no “bad blood” between the two sides. Jay Glazer’s initial report on Fox’s pregame show Sunday said that Jennings had scuttled the deal and turned down an offer to FaceTime with 49ers brass. Shanahan said that wasn’t true. “We talked for a while,” Shanahan said. “He FaceTimed me. … It was a good talk. But he’s with good people, he likes where he’s at and I thought it made sense what he said.” It’s safe to say that of the two former 49ers receivers, Jennings is in better standing than Aiyuk. “We love Jauan,” Shanahan said. “We have such a good relationship with Jauan and know him real well. away.headline: Ravens to trade for Jacoby Brissett from Cardinals to fill QB void: Report
away.blurb: Ravens to trade for QB Jacoby Brissett from Cardinals: Report – NBC New York Skip to content Main Navigation Search Search for: Weather Baltimore lost Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley to potential season-ending injuries last week. By Logan Reardon • Published November 4, 2026 • Updated on November 4, 2026 at 3:15 pm Jacoby Brissett of the Arizona Cardinals warms up prior to an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on Nov. 1, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. There's a new quarterback in Baltimore. Days after Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley suffered potential season-ending injuries , the Ravens reportedly traded for veteran Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and ESPN's Adam Schefter reported the news on Wednesday, adding that the trade is expected to be finalized over the weekend. Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano will start for Baltimore against Jacksonville, with inexperienced quarterbacks Austin Reed and Kedon Slovis serving as the backups. home.blurb: Macdonald clarified it is the quad injury, not the cracked rib, keeping Darnold out of Week 9 action. Drew Lock is dealing with an elbow injury but if available is slated to start with Jalen Milroe backing him up against the Cardinals, Macdonald said. The Seahawks don't currently have any other quarterbacks on the roster. Macdonald didn't rule out the possibility of adding another signal caller ahead of Sunday's game. The Seahawks first listed Lock on the injury report as limited with a right forearm issue ahead of a Week 6 loss at the Denver Broncos. Lock was listed as limited with a right elbow injury the following week before he was ruled out of a Week 7 win over the visiting Kansas City Chiefs. Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold will be sidelined with a quad injury for Sunday's matchup against the visiting Arizona Cardinals, head coach Mike Macdonald announced Wednesday. Darnold is considered week-to-week but won't be placed on IR, according to Macdonald. 7 Backup QBs Starting in Week 9 Darnold cracked a rib on the second play of Monday's loss to the Chicago Bears before suffering the quad injury late in the game, according to Macdonald. Darnold has started seven games for the Seahawks this season, completing 60.2 percent of his passes with 1,478 yards and 10 touchdowns alongside nine interceptions. Lock started in Weeks 2 and 3 after Darnold suffered a glute injury in his team's season opener. He most recently served as the Seahawks' emergency third quarterback against the Bears while Milroe backed up Darnold. Macdonald said after the Oct. 25 game the Seahawks didn't yet know the severity of Lock's injury but that it was "best for us right now to try to calm it down the best we can." As of Wednesday, Macdonald said Lock was "able to throw" but that his capacity would be determined during practice this week. Milroe has yet to see game action this season. He took just three snaps across three different contests during his rookie campaign with the Seahawks. The Seahawks (4-4) are currently deadlocked with the Los Angeles Rams for second in the NFC West behind the San Francisco 49ers (6-1). home.headline: They didn’t have to tell us that, definitely unusual — NFL analyst questions Seahawks’ decision to reveal Sam Darnold’s surprise injury
home.blurb: The Seattle Seahawks will be without Sam Darnold for their Week 9 matchup against the Arizona Cardinals, but the timing of the team’s announcement seems questionable to some, especially given its decision to disclose the quarterback’s injuries. “So they got a lot of faith in Drew Lock. I just think that this idea that Wednesday, out of the blue, they tell us that Sam Darnold is out with a quad injury. They tell us that he’s week to week, which usually means you’re going to miss a couple of weeks. They didn’t have to tell us that,” Florio said. “Now I appreciate the transparency, because what they could have done, they could have just put him down as did not practice. They could have done that yesterday. They could have done it today. They could have done it tomorrow, and then they could have called him out on Friday,” the analyst continued. Drew Lock is expected to start against Arizona, although his availability for Seattle is not settled. The veteran is managing a right-elbow injury and was listed as limited on Wednesday’s estimated injury report after Seattle held a walkthrough. Darnold, meanwhile, is considered week-to-week and has not been placed on injured reserve. The cracked rib could potentially be managed while playing, but the quad injury is expected to keep him out against Arizona. Coach Mike Macdonald confirmed Wednesday that Darnold would miss Sunday’s game because of a quad injury suffered late in Seattle’s 34-17 loss to the Chicago Bears. Mike Florio Questions Seahawks’ Decision To Announce Sam Darnold’s Absence Early While the coach disclosed the injury, Macdonald also revealed that the quarterback had played through a cracked rib for nearly the entire game. Darnold suffered the injury on the second play against Chicago after taking a hard hit from blitzing cornerback Kyler Gordon. He did not report the issue to the coaching or medical staff during the game and continued playing through the final whistle. He finished with two touchdown passes despite the injury, and Seattle’s coaches and medical staff did not learn about the cracked rib until after the game. The decision to reveal the extent of Darnold’s injuries, however, prompted NFL analyst Mike Florio to question why Seattle chose to announce the quarterback’s absence on Wednesday rather than wait until later in the week. Speaking on “NFL on NBC” with Chris Simms, Florio said the Seahawks could have followed the league’s injury reporting rules without immediately confirming that Darnold would miss Sunday’s game. “But they decided to just lead with their chin on this, which I thought was strange. It’s definitely unusual, and it forfeits the uncertainty that the Cardinals would have as to who they’re getting ready for. Now they know they’re getting ready for Drew Lock or Jalen Milroe,” Florio added. Chicago has not lost a game that Williams has started and finished this season (4-0), and it upset the Seattle Seahawks on Monday night in Week 8. The Bears have also scored at least 30 points in every game that Williams has completed this season, making them one of the most dangerous offenses in the league. picks.blurb: Buccaneers vs. Bears bold predictions for NFL Week 9 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football TNF: Jaguars-Ravens preview Wemby makes NBA history Ronaldo retires from Portugal Luka gets fan booted First CFP rankings Buccaneers vs. Bears bold predictions for NFL Week 9 Garrett Kerman, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Tue, November 3, 2026 at 6:02 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Chicago Bears meet on Sunday Night Football with very different momentum and very different identities. Tampa Bay just beat Atlanta 16–0 without completing a pass. Chicago comes in off an upset of Seattle. The Bears are 6-point favorites, and the total is 46.5. The Bucs have won three of their last four after an 0–4 start, so they are still in the NFC South race. These predictions lean on the contrast between Tampa Bay's run-first plan and Chicago's explosive offense. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Caleb Williams leads the Bears past 30 points again Credit: Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images Chicago will score at least 30 points, and Williams will account for three touchdowns. The Bears have scored 30 or more in every game Williams has finished this season, and they have not lost one he has started and finished (4–0). Since he returned from his hamstring injury, they have not trailed in any of three games. Williams threw for 308 yards and two touchdowns in a 30–24 win over New England. Chicago's pass offense averages 236.4 yards a game compared with 131.4 for Tampa Bay. That edge in the air is the core of this call. Tampa Bay's pass defense gives up 205.9 yards a game, which leaves room for chunk plays. Chicago's offense ranks 10th in EPA per play despite Williams missing three full games. I expect him to throw for at least 275 yards and add a rushing score. The one wrinkle is the Bears' backfield. Running back Kyle Monangai is listed as out with a thumb injury, which could shift more of the offense to Williams. Tampa Bay runs for 200 yards and still loses The Bucs will pile up another 200 rushing yards, and it still won't be enough. Against Atlanta, Tampa Bay ran 56 times for 324 yards. Bucky Irving gained 170 yards on 27 carries, and Kenny Gainwell added 140 on 25. Baker Mayfield attempted only three passes in steady rain. Chicago's run defense is beatable, allowing 4.4 yards per carry. Tampa Bay ranks eighth in EPA per rush, so the ground game will work on Sunday night. The problem is what happens when Chicago scores early. The Bucs average 22.3 points a game. A team rated poorly through the air can't easily come back against the best third-down defense in football, according to one projection. I'm projecting 200 rushing yards because the Bears' run defense can't stop everything. But Tampa Bay's offense needs scoring drives, not just yards, and the run game alone won't produce 30 points. Injuries make it harder. Gainwell is questionable with a hip issue, and outside linebacker Yaya Diaby was trending toward out. Wide receiver Emeka Egbuka was inactive last week with a foot injury and is also a concern. Mayfield throws 35 passes and the Bears win 34–20 The game ends with Chicago winning 34–20, and Mayfield forced into a very different afternoon than the one in Tampa. A 34–20 final would add up to 54 points, clearing the 46.5 total comfortably, and it would give Chicago a 14-point cover. Mayfield returned from a fractured thumb two games ago and is still working back to full rhythm. He has 679 passing yards and three touchdowns on the season, so asking him to throw 35 times is a real shift for this offense. That volume creates risk. If Chicago leads by two scores in the third quarter, Tampa Bay has to abandon the run and put the ball in Mayfield's hands. I expect two interceptions, including one that sets up a Chicago touchdown. The Bucs will compete. They'll move the ball, their kicker has been perfect this season and their defense will make a few plays. But the Bears' offense is more dangerous, and they are better built to play with a lead. picks.headline: Week 9 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Bears have momentum going into Sunday night vs. Buccaneers
picks.blurb: Week 9 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Bears have momentum going into Sunday night vs. Buccaneers - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football TNF: Jaguars-Ravens preview Wemby makes NBA history Ronaldo retires from Portugal Luka gets fan booted First CFP rankings Frank Schwab Senior writer Thu, November 5, 2026 at 7:30 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Chicago Bears hype is about to get very loud. This NFL season seems wide open. There isn't one great team yet and there are few trustworthy contenders who have emerged. The Bears seemingly saw it the same way when they traded two first-round picks for defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons. And through one game, it seems like a transformative trade. The Bears had a fantastic performance on a national stage, shutting down the Seahawks in a 34-17 win . Chicago's Super Bowl odds took a leap, as did Caleb Williams' MVP odds. In a season dying for a dominant team to emerge, maybe it's Chicago. The Bears' offense isn't a question. It has scored 30 points in every game Williams has started and finished (it did score just three points against the Vikings and Williams played three-and-a-half quarters, but that says something about Minnesota's defense). If Simmons has as big of an impact on the defense as it appeared on Monday night, Chicago will be looking really good. Nobody paying attention to the NFL hadn't seen how dominant Simmons is, but it was still impressive to see how quickly he fit in and made plays. Chicago gets another close-up in prime time this week against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday night. Surprisingly, the Buccaneers are far better analytically than their 3-5 record would suggest. They're fifth in DVOA , eight spots ahead of the Bears, and eight in net EPA (expected points added) per play. The Bears are strong in net EPA, coming in third. The Buccaneers will be completely overshadowed in this game. The Bears will be the focus on Sunday night as they've emerged as one of the NFL's most dangerous teams. That's a reason they're a healthy 6.5-point favorite. That's a lot of points, and the Buccaneers might be secretly pretty good. That's why Buccaneers +6.5 is the pick. And if the Bears blow out Tampa Bay in a big prime-time window, they'll take over as the talk of the NFL, if they're not already. The Bears are 4-0 in games that Caleb Williams started and finished this season. Here are the rest of the picks against the spread for Week 9 of the NFL season: Jaguars (-10) over Ravens Even at -10, the line seems too low. The Jaguars have three wins by 24 points or more and two came against the 5-3 Browns and the 5-3 Patriots. They're good. There could be a letdown facing Baltimore undrafted rookie quarterback Joe Fagnano, and it's possible the Ravens rally around Fagnano for a season-saving performance with Jacoby Brissett on the way next week. But this seems like a huge ask for the Ravens, who have scored 13 or fewer points in three straight games. Bengals (-3) over Falcons The Bengals and Falcons go to Madrid, Spain, for this one. The Falcons are nearly impossible to figure out. They followed up a win over the undefeated 49ers by losing to a Buccaneers team that didn't complete a pass. That sums up Atlanta's season. We should trust Joe Burrow, who is on a heater, though there are more questions about Cincinnati's defense after it gave up 36 points to the Titans at home last week. Giants (-3) over Eagles Maybe Joe Milton III gives Philadelphia a boost and the Eagles get their first win since Week 2. But since Jalen Hurts went on IR, the Eagles have lost all three games by double digits. It's not a good team in any way, and Milton is far from a sure thing. The Giants are off a bye and should be feeling good coming into this one. Panthers (+2.5) over Broncos The Broncos are the better team. A few things work against them in this spot: It's an early start on the East Coast, and the Panthers have three days rest advantage. The Broncos are also coming off an emotional win over the Chiefs and there could be a letdown. Denver has been much better at home this season. Carolina has faded after a good start but this is a decent opportunity for a win. Dolphins (+7) over Lions Give Miami credit for playing hard. Maybe at some point that effort starts to fade, but the last time they truly got blown out was Week 2. They lost by 14 points to the Chiefs, but Kansas City led by only seven points with three minutes left. It's possible the Lions score enough to cover, but remember that they're usually a different team outdoors. Chiefs (-10) over Jets Kansas City will enjoy the breather after facing the Seattle and Denver defenses on the road the past two weeks. This seems like the type of game in which the Chiefs could take out their frustrations on an opponent that does have some talent but has won only once since Week 1. Saints (-3) over Browns The Browns are likely going with Shedeur Sanders at quarterback because Deshaun Watson was put in concussion protocol. It's not like Watson was playing so well he's irreplaceable, but Sanders has thrown only three passes all season. The Saints are well rested coming off a bye. The Saints are not a great team this season, but this might be a spot for them to get right. Rams (-5.5) over Commanders Is it time to trust the Rams? They have covered two games in a row without a sweat. Those wins came against mediocre (Raiders) or bad (Chargers) teams, but they did handle business. And the Commanders are mediocre at best and maybe just bad. Let's see if the Rams are truly back. Cowboys (-5.5) over Colts It is incredibly hard to trust the Cowboys, especially as a road favorite. But what we saw from the Colts last week in a 42-7 loss was troubling. There was no fight left in that team, which has lost key players to trades and knows its season is done. This could be a bad mistake, trusting a defense that can't stop anyone to cover almost a touchdown on the road. Taking the Colts at this point is even harder. Texans (-4.5) over Chargers It's a lot for Houston to be favored by this much on the road, however, home-field advantage has been mostly eliminated this NFL season and the Chargers have no home-field advantage — even if that was still a thing. Houston is coming off a bye and still has hopes to revive its season. The Texans still have a 34.4% chance to make the playoffs according to DVOA. The Chargers are 0.0% on that list. They'll cover a spread at some point but it's hard to anticipate when it happens. Raiders (+10) over 49ers The Raiders have four losses, and they came against four of the better teams in the NFL: Chiefs, Patriots, Bills and Rams. The bad news is this week they get the Super Bowl favorites. The 49ers should be getting many players back after their bye. But the Raiders can move the ball and they're getting a lot of points. Seahawks (-8.5) over Cardinals With all the quarterback chaos this week, we get two teams that had a different quarterback in Week 8. Brissett was benched and traded, and Gardner Minshew II takes over. Sam Darnold has a quad injury and he'll be out, with Drew Lock taking over. Lock is a reasonable replacement, and Minshew isn't facing the Cowboys defense this week. Packers (+3) over Patriots The Patriots have a lot of injuries and the Packers have a few days of extra rest. In a game that seems evenly matched, the small edges add up. Green Bay started the season very slow but has looked much better over the last four games, winning three and barely losing at Detroit. New England has also emerged after an early-season slump to win four of five. This is a really fun matchup, and even enough to feel OK taking the points. Vikings (+3.5) over Bills This is an interesting game because the teams have opposite strengths. The Bills have a great offense and bad defense, and the Vikings have a bad offense and great defense. The Minnesota defense held the Bears to three points after all; Chicago has scored 30 points in every other Caleb Williams start. It will be a great test against Josh Allen, who is having another fantastic season. It's never enjoyable to be going against Allen, but getting 3.5 points with a defense this good seems right … as long as the offense does at least a little bit. Last week : 7-7 Season to date: 53-65-2

picks.headline: Buccaneers, Bears: Week 9 game preview
picks.blurb: Buccaneers, Bears: Week 9 game preview - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football TNF: Jaguars-Ravens preview Wemby makes NBA history Ronaldo retires from Portugal Luka gets fan booted First CFP rankings Buccaneers, Bears: Week 9 game preview TAMPA, FLORIDA - SEPTEMBER 17: Baker Mayfield #6 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers attempts a pass during the first quarter against the Chicago Bears at Raymond James Stadium on September 17, 2023 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Julio Aguilar/Getty Images) | Getty Images Will Walsh · SB Nation Thu, November 5, 2026 at 1:01 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Anyone watch Monday Night Football? Wow, the Bears look good. Ben Johnson, Caleb Williams, and their Chicago Bears seem like they are on a collision course for a deep playoff run in 2026. So yes, the Bears are hot— Steaming, but so are the Buccaneers. Tampa Bay is coming off two-straight wins, three of their last four and has seemingly found their new formula for offensive success. Will those good vibes and momentum carry over into the Chicago night on Sunday Night Football? " Battles are won in the trenches, in the grit and grime of courageous determination. " How can the Buccaneers win? Be the line they claim to be. TAMPA, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 1: Graham Barton #62 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers blocks against Kendal Daniels #53 of the Atlanta Falcons during the first half of the game at Raymond James Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chicago Bears are no joke and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers will need to be all the way buttoned up to be able to stay with Chicago in this game. The Bears have a lot of things going for them in 2026, but their most recent addition may be the scariest. Chicago's highly publicized trade for Jeffery Simmons opened some eyes when they made it. For those who haven't seen may Titans' games over the years, Monday night may have opened some more— Simmons is in the elite class of football players in the NFL and after spending years on a losing team, he looks motivated and rejuvenated. The trade for Simmons was an all-in move, the kind of move teams make when they have one goal on their mind— The Bears are a Super Bowl or bust team. The trade paid immediate dividends, Simmons' first game with Chicago was a watch what I can do performance as he snared a team-leading six tackles (two for a loss) and a sack. For the Buccaneers, this game will be the game where their offensive line needs to prove the last two weeks true. Tampa's season began horrifically, 0-4, a quarterback injury, and more importantly for the sake of this discussion, an offensive line that was woeful. Tampa Bay's offensive line came into the season projected to be one of the strongest units on the team, perhaps in the league, depending on who you asked. Through the first four games, the Buccaneers allowed 20 sacks. Baker Mayfield spent most of those first four games running in circles behind the line of scrimmage like Fran Tarkenton, until he ran himself into an injury. In the four since, Tampa's only surrendered seven sacks with five of the seven coming against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Tampa Bay will be and should be the underdog on Sunday. If there is any chance that an upset is in the cards they will need to protect their quarterback. Baker Mayfield is going to have to attempt more than three passes in this game to lead the team to victory and he will need to be upright to do so. Chicago has an absolute game-wrecker on their defense, he will make his plays— The Bucs can't expect to wipe Jeffery Simmons out of the game, however, they cannot allow the game to devolve into what fans saw earlier in the season from this offensive line, Baker Mayfield, and the passing game. " You can't stop him, you can only hope to contain him ." How can the Buccaneers lose? Lose contain of Caleb Williams. Caleb Williams might not be a truly great quarterback, though he does seem to be enroute to that status in short order, but he is a truly special athlete. No, he isn't running 4.2 40's or leaping 13' in a broad jump but he is as all around dynamic as they come. One of the issues Tampa Bay might have is Williams simply does not throw interceptions. Caleb has missed some time this year, but he has only thrown one interception— Last year, just seven. Williams' lack of interceptions isn't even a Ben Johnson related statistic because dating back two years ago, pre their union, Williams tossed just six while throwing 20 touchdowns for a better than 3:1 touchdown to interception ratio. In his career (three years), Williams has thrown less interceptions than Baker Mayfield did in 2024—Turnovers may be off the table. Another key issue that Caleb Williams presents is his elite management of the pocket. Williams is not a runner, but he is quite mobile. He has a phenomenal ability to majestically glide up, back, or out of the pocket towards free space and away from danger . Todd Bowles and the Buccaneers' defense will need to work tirelessly to mitigate that on Sunday night. Williams will dagger the Bucs with big plays off script if they let him. Bowles and the Bucs have been somewhat of mixed bag against mobile quarterbacks, different matchups bringing about different results, but Caleb Williams will represent a very unique challenge. Williams is not just looking to move around the pocket to buy time to throw— He isn't just looking break out of the pocket so that he heave the ball down field on a broken play— He won't be looking to run outside of contain so that he can scramble for yards to move the chains— Caleb Williams will be looking to do any and all of the above. He is special and he has proven that he can do each and every one of those things on any given play— Meaning, the Buccaneers must be dialed into the details on their rushes, sound in their tackling, and if they are caught lacking and take even just one snap off Williams could gash them for a game changing play. Todd Bowles' defense has been reliably solid in 2026, as of late they've been exemplary. Sunday night's game against Chicago will be a true test. Caleb Williams has the ability to put a defense on a poster, he and Ben Johnson have left a decent amount of carnation in their wake. Can Tampa Bay contain Caleb Williams and stay off his highlight reel?

picks.headline: Buccaneers at Bears: Predictions, picks and odds for NFL Week 9 game
picks.blurb: Chicago's rolling with Caleb Williams back. The Bears have won three straight since his return from a hamstring injury, scoring at least 30 points in each game without ever trailing. That includes Monday's 34-17 win in Seattle. Chicago has won those games by an average of 10.3 points. Who needs a passing game? Tampa Bay beat Atlanta 16-0 last week without completing a single pass, rushing for a franchise-record 324 yards. Bucky Irving contributed 170 yards and Kenny Gainwell added 140. That followed a 30-point blowout of the Panthers in which Baker Mayfield only threw for 64 yards, as the ground-attack generated 258 yards. Third-down could decide this one. Chicago's defense has held opponents to a league-best 23.8% conversion rate. Getting Tampa Bay into obvious passing situations would put pressure on an offense with the NFL's lowest team passer rating. Swift enters with momentum. D'Andre Swift scored three second-half rushing touchdowns against Seattle. Chicago's ability to finish drives on the ground gives Williams valuable support near the goal line. Watch the turnaround and the number. Chicago returns from a Monday night road game to host Sunday night. The Bears are favored in the -6/-6.5 range, a sizable margin against a Buccaneers team coming off consecutive wins. Under Ben Johnson, Chicago is 8-1 against the spread in primetime games. Todd Bowles, however, is just 11-18 straight-up and 10-18-1 ATS in that spot as head coach of the Bucs and Jets. Bears vs Buccaneers odds, moneyline, over/under Opening lines: Spread: Bears -6.5 Moneyline: Bears -270; Buccaneers +225 Get the edge with our exclusive NFL betting picks Bears vs Buccaneers USA TODAY expert picks Adam Kaufman: Bears 27, Buccaneers 20 Tampa Bay just won a game without completing a pass. Fun fact. Probably not the blueprint you want to carry into every Sunday. Chicago is playing with confidence, Caleb Williams looks increasingly comfortable and Ben Johnson's offense has enough balance to avoid making this entirely about the quarterback. The Buccaneers' defense can absolutely create problems, especially if Williams gets careless under pressure, but I expect Chicago to make Tampa Bay sustain more offense than it needed against Atlanta. The Bears' shorter week after visiting Seattle keeps me from projecting a runaway. Still, they should do enough to win a fourth straight and cover the number. Michael Middlehurst-Schwartz: Bears 31, Buccaneers 16 Todd Bowles might need to conjure another storm to even the playing field. The Buccaneers will surely need more than a 0-3 passing performance from Baker Mayfield to keep up with one of the NFC's most imposing matchups. away.headline: Buccaneers get a major boost from latest injury report ahead of Week 8 vs. Falcons
away.blurb: Fortunately, the Buccaneers received some encouraging news on the injury front just in time for the pivotal matchup. Several key players are trending toward a return, giving Tampa Bay a chance to take the field with its healthiest roster in weeks. The Buccaneers released their injury report after practice on Thursday, and several designations stood out. Antoine Winfield Jr. was a full participant after missing the last three games with a fractured rib , and the star safety is gearing up for a return. Heading into a matchup against a stacked Falcons offense featuring Bijan Robinson, Drake London and Kyle Pitts, the importance of Winfield's return can't be overstated. Emeka Egbuka, who missed last week due to a concussion and foot injury, was a limited participant and has a chance to play against the Falcons. But Irving and Godwin were each given rest days, so Goedeke is the only player truly out with an injury as things currently stand. All in all, it’s hard not to be encouraged with Winfield making his return and Egbuka having a chance to do the same. Both teams will be overwhelmingly healthy entering Week 8, so there are no excuses. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers’ showdown with the Atlanta Falcons in Week 8 will make or break the season, and the Bucs need all hands on deck to keep their playoff hopes alive. Buccaneers get encouraging injury news at the perfect time ahead of Falcons showdown Josiah Trotter, who missed practice earlier in the week due to an illness, returned as a full particplant on Thursday. Kenny Gainwell, coming off his best game as a Buccaneer with 88 rushing yards, returned to practice after missing Wednesday with a hip injury. Tampa Bay is getting healthy at the perfect time. Luke Goedeke could be Buccaneers' only key absence in Week 8 The only three players who didn’t practice were Luke Goedeke, Bucky Irving and Chris Godwin Jr. While being without their premier starting right tackle is far from ideal, the Bucs’ offense operated just fine with Benjamin Chukwuma as the starting right tackle last week. In fact, it was their best performance of the year, allowing zero sacks and rushing for 258 total yards. Todd Bowles went on the record saying that Chukwuma has a “huge future” as an NFL starter , so the coaching staff has the utmost confidence in him as the next-man up. home.headline: Kyle Monangai Injury Update & Everything Else From Bears' Thursday Practice Report
home.blurb: The Chicago Bears' Thursday practice report is out and it has both good news and bad news for the Bears ahead of their Week 9 game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday. Good news for left tackle Theo Benedet and defensive tackle Grady Jarrett, as both were upgraded from non-participants to limited. T.J. Edwards was upgraded, also, but his lack of participation Wednesday wasn't injury-related. With Benedet and Jarrett getting in a limited session, that puts them back on track to suit up. With Monangai failing to practice yet again, we can pretty much rule him out for Week 9 already, which means another week of Roschon Johnson filling in as RB2. Kyle Monangai Injury Update From ESPN Gives Bears RB Shred of Hope For Week 8 Return The bad news comes from the fact that two players on the injury report didn't see any progress from yesterday's estimated version , and Chicago saw a new addition with linebacker D'Marco Jackson. The good news is that two other players who were estimated non-participants to start the week saw an uptick in participation on Thursday. Now, a full look at the injury report. Earlier in the day, offensive coordinator Press Taylor sounded optimistic that Ozzy Trapilo would be ready to play a full complement of snaps if Benedet can't go. "I feel pretty good about the path we've put him on to be able to do that if needed," Taylor said, according to Sean Hammond of The Chicago Tribune . The new addition, Jackson, is dealing with an ankle injury. He was listed on last week's injury report with an ankle issue, but it isn't clear if it's the same one. Monangai injury update, more Bears RB woes The Bears willl have a new RB3, though, as Zavier Scott was placed on injured reserve earlier in the day with a thumb injury. Scott will miss at least the next four games, and that is all he is expected to miss, per Brad Biggs of The Chicago Tribune . When it comes to who will replace Scott, the only other healthy back on the roster other than Swift and Johnson is Salvon Ahmed, who was one of the Bears' standouts during the offseason. We could see Chicago add another back to the practice squad, but Ahmed will likely be the guy who gets the nod for Week 9. home.headline: Chicago Bears coach gets honest on Cole Kmet, Sam Roush issue
home.blurb: The Chicago Bears have big shoes to fill at tight end after Cole Kmet suffered a season-ending knee injury in the team’s 30-24 win over the New England Patriots in Week 7. The Bears had one of the better tight end rooms in the league with Colston Loveland, Kmet, and rookie Sam Roush. Chicago also has Stephen Carlson on the 53-man roster. During his news conference on Thursday, Bears offensive coordinator Press Taylor gave an honest assessment about the team’s plans at tight end going forward. He said the Bears would have to come up with a new game plan every week, and there wasn’t one tight end that can take the role that Kmet had for the offense. “That is going to change week to week,” Taylor said , via CHGO Bears. “ “There is not one guy who is going to do what Cole did.” The Chicago Bears need Sam Roush to improve Through the first seven games, Kmet recorded 10 receptions for 87 yards and one touchdown. He has been a key part of the blocking scheme. Loveland has been the top pass catcher at the position, hauling in 33 receptions for 309 yards and two scores. Taylor was asked what Roush needed to do to earn more targets. Taylor noted that the Bears have a lot of options for quarterback Caleb Williams, but the team is happy where the third-round pick is right now. “We have a lot of mouths to feed,” Taylor said . “We are really happy with the progress he has made and where he is going.” Roush has three catches for 33 yards this season. He wasn’t expected to be a big part of the passing game when he was drafted, but offered the offense another blocking tight end and someone who could help with 13 personnel and special teams. At best, the results have been mixed for Roush in his rookie season. With Kmet gone for the season, the Bears will need Roush to develop a little quicker. Want more articles like this? picks.headline: Bills vs. Vikings bold predictions for Week 9 Monday Night Football
picks.blurb: Bills vs. Vikings bold predictions for Week 9 Monday Night Football - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football TNF: Jaguars-Ravens preview Wemby makes NBA history Ronaldo retires from Portugal Luka gets fan booted First CFP rankings Bills vs. Vikings bold predictions for Week 9 Monday Night Football Garrett Kerman, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Tue, November 3, 2026 at 5:57 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Two 6-1 teams enter Monday Night Football with very different questions. Can the Buffalo Bills keep rolling against the NFL's stingiest defense? Can the Minnesota Vikings generate enough offense to avoid wasting another strong defensive performance? Buffalo visits U.S. Bank Stadium on November 9 following a 36–10 victory over Baltimore. Minnesota returns home after Detroit ended its unbeaten start with a 19–15 win. The Bills opened as three-point favorites, setting up a compelling clash between offensive firepower and defensive disruption. These three predictions anticipate a departure from Minnesota's usual defensive script, explosive passing, costly mistakes and a dramatic finish that hands Buffalo its second defeat. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Justin Jefferson explodes for 175 yards and two touchdowns Matt Krohn-Imagn Images Jefferson will deliver the performance Minnesota has been waiting for, finishing with at least 175 receiving yards and two touchdowns. Jefferson caught five passes for 33 yards and a touchdown against Detroit and enters Week 9 without a 100-yard receiving game. Buffalo presents an opportunity to change that. Its defense ranks 30th against the pass, making this a matchup Minnesota should attack rather than approach conservatively. The Vikings need to manufacture touches before asking Jefferson to win difficult downfield assignments. Motion, condensed formations and crossing routes would help create cleaner releases and give the quarterback defined throwing windows. The bigger gains should follow when Buffalo adjusts to those shorter completions. One double move or broken coverage could turn a productive evening into a spectacular one. Quarterback availability remains important. Kyler Murray is managing hamstring tightness , with Carson Wentz the likely alternative if Murray cannot play. Expect Minnesota to make its best receiver the centerpiece, not merely a name opponents must account for. Josh Allen accounts for four touchdowns but commits three turnovers Allen will produce enough spectacular plays to keep Buffalo dangerous and enough mistakes to give Minnesota control of the outcome. The bold prediction is four total touchdowns alongside three turnovers, including at least two interceptions. https://twitter.com/search?q=josh%20allen&src=typed_query&f=top Minnesota's defense provides the foundation for that aggressive forecast. Entering Week 9, the Vikings lead the league in points allowed per game at 13.3, quarterback pressure rate at 45.8 percent and sack percentage at 10.96 percent. Pressure alone will not neutralize Allen. His ability to escape the pocket can turn a successful blitz into a defensive emergency, particularly when coverage players must chase receivers across the field. That creates the central tension. Minnesota will win several snaps decisively, but Allen will punish a few failed pressure attempts with explosive completions or scrambling opportunities. The turnovers will come when he tries to rescue plays that should end with a throwaway. Disguised coverage behind an apparent blitz can invite exactly that kind of aggressive decision. Buffalo's offensive line also bears watching. Right tackle Spencer Brown's availability is a concern entering the matchup, potentially complicating protection against Minnesota's pressure packages. Allen will remain the game's most dangerous improviser. On this night, improvisation will carry a substantial price. Minnesota wins 38–35 on a last-second field goal The final bold prediction ties those individual performances together: Minnesota wins a shootout with a field goal as time expires. A 38–35 result would produce 73 points, comfortably exceeding the opening total of 46.5. It would also represent a dramatic departure from the Vikings' defensive scoring average. The logic is not that Minnesota suddenly becomes a bad defense. Turnovers and explosive plays can produce points without requiring long, methodical drives. Jefferson's breakout keeps the Vikings moving, while Allen repeatedly answers before one late mistake gives Minnesota the deciding possession. After losing its unbeaten record, Minnesota will respond with its most convincing offensive statement and a victory that reinforces its place among the league's contenders. picks.headline: Minnesota Vikings Receive Bold Prediction for Game Against Buffalo Bills
picks.blurb: Minnesota Vikings Receive Bold Prediction for Game Against Buffalo Bills - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football TNF: Jaguars-Ravens preview Wemby makes NBA history Ronaldo retires from Portugal Luka gets fan booted First CFP rankings Minnesota Vikings Receive Bold Prediction for Game Against Buffalo Bills (Gregory Fisher-USA TODAY Sports) Joey Hickey · Roundtable Sports Thu, November 5, 2026 at 6:00 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Minnesota Vikings (6-1) have a pivotal matchup on Monday Night Football against the Buffalo Bills. And while losing the game wouldn't make them a pretender, winning the game could solidify the Vikings as contenders. Minnesota has played great defense through seven games, but the offense has been lacking. Now, fans are looking for the team to show improvement on offense. If it doesn't happen, we could see the team explore changes on offense. Vikings Wire's Andrew Harbaugh predicts that Vikings backup quarterback Carson Wentz will see playing time in Monday night's game against the Buffalo Bills. Here's some of what Harbaugh had to say about his chances to take the field for Minnesota in the game. "Kyler Murray has played poorly enough this season and has not shown a real grasp of the offense or the players' tendencies within it. Carson Wentz has not been a rockstar, but he has been more than serviceable for the Vikings when he has played. I predict that the first half could be rough for the Vikings' offense, and at halftime Kevin O'Connell tries to give the offense a spark with a quarterback change." Harbaugh adds that it could be a breakout day for another Vikings player. He has star Vikings wideout Justin Jefferson catching two touchdown passes in the matchup. Here's what he had to say on the breakout. "Justin Jefferson has started to be a bit more vocal about how he feels about the offense being so quiet. I think they make it a point to get him going early in the game, and then by the end of the night he has two touchdowns. They have to get him involved more; the offense goes as Justin Jefferson goes, after all. If they do not use him more soon, then ideas and outside voices are going to start getting louder." Jefferson's frustrations have drawn questions about the player throwing him the football. It's not surprising that there have been questions given all the pieces that the Vikings have on offense. It's not that starting quarterback Kyler Murray has been awful. The offense has been awful, though. Some believe a change at quarterback is necessary to bring a spark. Maybe a change at quarterback isn't the fix, but something will need to change for the offense to start moving the football. If it doesn't the Vikings will have squandered what could be one of the NFL's best defenses of the last decade. We'll keep a close eye on what moves head coach Kevin O'Connell makes when the matchup gets underway with Buffalo.

picks.headline: NFL Insider Makes Bold Prediction About Vikings Offensive Direction in Week 9 vs. Bills
picks.blurb: NFL Insider Makes Bold Prediction About Vikings Offensive Direction in Week 9 vs. Bills - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football TNF: Jaguars-Ravens preview Wemby makes NBA history Ronaldo retires from Portugal Luka gets fan booted First CFP rankings Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kevin O'Connell has spent the week calling Kyler Murray his starter, but a hamstring may make that call for him. NFL Network insider Tom Pelissero said Thursday on KFAN's Power Trip Morning Show that he expects Carson Wentz to start for the 6-1 Minnesota Vikings against the Buffalo Bills on Monday night, days after Murray struggled through the loss in Detroit . "I would lean toward it being Carson Wentz," Pelissero said on KFAN . He described the hamstring as legitimate but not major, and said Minnesota may not want to risk a quarterback who relies on his legs at less than full speed. Carson Wentz has already won two games Nov 1, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Minnesota Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell talks to quarterback Kyler Murray (1) during the third quarter against the Detroit Lions at Ford Field.Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images Wentz isn't a stranger to this offense. He played most of the 39-22 opener against Green Bay after replacing Murray early and threw three touchdown passes, then started the 9-3 win in Chicago. He has 276 passing yards and no interceptions this season, and Minnesota won both games. Those wins weren't pretty, though. The offense scored nine points at Soldier Field, and Wentz was sacked six times across the two games. Behind a line that has allowed 21 sacks, the Vikings would be trading mobility for a quarterback who has to get the ball out on time. Murray has 1,022 passing yards, five touchdown passes and three interceptions, and he's been sacked 15 times. He has also run for 167 yards on 29 carries, which is why a sore hamstring matters more for him than it would for most quarterbacks. O'Connell said Monday he isn't considering a performance benching and Murray is still the starter when healthy, per ESPN. "I don't think we're there yet," he said of a possible absence , adding that he would keep getting updates from the medical staff. Pelissero's take lands after Nick Kostos argued the Vikings can't keep waiting on Murray . Pelissero also said he sees a low chance of a major trade before the Nov. 10 deadline, which leaves the job between the two quarterbacks already in the building. Either one draws a tough assignment. Buffalo's Greg Rousseau has seven sacks, and Josh Allen brings the NFL's most efficient offense to U.S. Bank Stadium, so Brian Flores' defense may need to carry the night again. O'Connell's Thursday press availability should offer the next clue. away.headline: Vikings’ Jauan Jennings joins Kyler Murray on injury report for Bills game
away.blurb: Now, the Vikings may be down without one of their wide receivers, as Jauan Jennings has popped up on the injury report with a calf injury. The good news is that he was limited on the first day of practice, and he still has two more days to show that he can play. The Minnesota Vikings will be facing the Buffalo Bills this week, and they could be without some of their key players for the matchup. There was already doubt surrounding Kyler Murray ’s status for the game, as he suffered a hamstring injury in their last game, and Carson Wentz is set to be QB1 against the Bills. Jennings hasn’t been very productive for the Vikings this season, as he only has 54 receiving yards. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) There was a chance that Jennings was going to be in a trade that sent him back to the San Francisco 49ers, but after a conversation with head coach Kyle Shanahan, they didn’t pursue the deal . “We love Jauan,” Shanahan said via ESPN’s Nick Wagoner. “We have such a good relationship with Jauan and know him real well, and we didn’t want to do it without talking to him first. So, we had to agree on some things to at least make it close enough to be able to talk to him. And when we got on a FaceTime with JJ, it went well. “We talked about a lot of stuff, and he ended up saying that he was happy with where he was. It wasn’t just like a definite no at first, but he was like, ‘Man, Kyle, I’m pretty happy here and liking stuff.'” It’s no surprise that Jennings didn’t want to get traded, especially with the Vikings playing some of the best football in the league. Kyler Murray Injury Update: NFL Insider Casts Doubt on Vikings QB's Status; Odds vs. Bills Shift Skip to main content ON SI Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray is up in the air for Week 9 against the Buffalo Bills due to a hamstring injury that he suffered in the team's Week 8 loss to the Detroit Lions. Earlier this week, Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell revealed that Murray is dealing with a hamstring issue and that he'd be re-evaluated this week. Murray and the Vikings don't play until Monday night in Week 9, so they have yet to release a practice report since their first official session will come on Thursday. That has left the quarterback's status in limbo with the Vikings (6-1) looking to remain in the top spot in the NFC North. NFL insider Ian Rapoport doesn't believe that Murray is dealing with a long-term injury, but he did mention that Murray may not play since he's a mobile quarterback and can't move around as well. That would pave the way for veteran Carson Wentz to get the start, something he did in place of Murray in Week 2. away.headline: Bills' Joe Brady shares WR DJ Moore injury update
away.blurb: When asked what it meant to him to be back out there, he was quick to respond. "Everything!" "Meant everything. I got the jitters when I first stepped on the field and then I got the jitters out even more when I fumbled and I was like, 'All right, now it's time to really lock back in and get going,'" the WR1 shared . "So, I was nervous at first and then went out there and just was like, 'All right, this is the game that I love and was good.'" Head coach Joe Brady spoke to the impact that Moore's return had as well as his importance to the Buffalo offense. He limped off the field after that play, and went to the medical tent to get checked out, before returning. Though he again showed a limp leaving the field after the game, he says he is okay. "You play a lot of games in this league. You're nervous because of coming back from the injury or just cuz you haven't been out there," he added. "It's more because of the injury and not being out there. So, l'm like, 'Dang, am I in game shape?' And today I found out I was." Allen went 8-19 and 112 yards passing in the air with an interception and two touchdowns, and rushed for a touchdown as well. One of the scoring throws went to Moore, to give Allen the franchise mark for passing TDs. He also found Moore on a big 40+ contested catch to put the Bills in scoring range. It was Moore's first game back after missing time for nearly a month due to a shoulder injury from an NFL week 4 matchup against the New England Patriots. He had four receptions for 82 yards and the touchdown in the win. "You can see what he does to our offense. He made some big plays for us, and you know it's going. It's obviously was great to get him back.", Brady said postgame. There was a scare that has brought Brady's decision to keep Moore in the game late after the Bills had a commanding lead. The receiver came down at an awkward angle landing off balance on his knee in the game, and taking a hit to the lower body while making a catch during a fourth-quarter drive. When asked about what the injury was, Moore said "Hyper extension. Yeah, we'd be good though." He also reassured that his body was in playing condition and in step with where it needed to feel in returning to game play. We may earn a commission when you buy through links on this page. home.source: The Minnesota Star Tribune on MSN
home.blurb: Murray was ruled out Thursday by head coach Kevin O’Connell due to a hamstring strain. O’Connell said he couldn’t project Darrisaw’s game status, but “early days of treatment here have been encouraging enough that we can get him out there and get him practicing a little bit today, and we’ll see how it goes.” The Vikings will be without quarterback Kyler Murray for their “Monday Night Football” matchup against the Buffalo Bills . Carson Wentz will start in Murray’s place ; Max Brosmer will be the backup. “For [Murray], his movement skills and the way he plays the game, we do feel like we’d be putting him at risk of possibly turning this into a more significant injury than it is by trying to have him work through it here early on,” O’Connell said. The Vikings could potentially also be without a key player on defense in safety Theo Jackson, who has a quad injury. O’Connell said Jackson would not practice Thursday. The Vikings have several safeties who could step up in Jackson’s place and are already flexible in how they play the position within Brian Flores’ defensive scheme. O’Connell referenced Jay Ward and undrafted free agent Jacob Thomas as possibilities to play more minutes alongside Josh Metellus and Harrison Smith . “[Ward’s] got a bunch of experience in the system,” O’Connell said. “We’ll take a look at it throughout the week if we want to possibly have another safety on the game day roster.” Safety Jakobe Thomas , a rookie third-round pick who’s yet to be active for a game, could be another option. Left tackle Christian Darrisaw is set to practice Thursday after coming in with shoulder soreness Monday. ©2026 The Minnesota Star Tribune. Visit startribune.com. home.headline: Vikings-Bills First Injury Report
home.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Vikings, Kyler Murray being out is the big news and he will not play on Monday night. Theo Jackson also did not practice on Thursday and seems more questionable whether he’ll play or not. Kevin O’Connell said they have other safeties like Jay Ward who could play in Jackson’s absence and a few others are possbilities to be active on Monday night if need be as well. The rest of the injuries appear to be more of the ‘playing through it’ variety and don’t seem like they’ll keep those players out on Monday night. For the Bills, a laundry list of players on the injury report including three offensive line starters. Starting left tackle Dion Dawkins did not practice Thursday with a rib injury, nor did starting guard Alec Andreesen, with an ankle injury. Right tackle Spencer Brown was limited with a back issue. We’ll see how it plays out with injury updates tomorrow and Saturday.
